author: re-marked
body:
## Bug (Mark live observation)

Mark's CEO during slumber: ONE long claude turn (text → tool → text → tool → text, 6 text blocks across 13 minutes) rendered as 6 separate timestamped chat bubbles. Made the CEO look like it was "waking up fresh" between blocks. Confirmed against the jsonl: only 1 user prompt, 1 long claude turn, multiple persisted text segments because v2.1.4's \`onAssistantText\` writes each block as its own JSONL message.

## Fix

Stamp every persisted message inside one harness dispatch with a shared \`metadata.turnId\` (generated once per dispatch via \`generateId()\`). MessageList groups consecutive same-sender messages with the same turnId — one header at the top, then text rows + tool rows interleaved inline. Tool events render as compact \`│ tool\` rows when inside a group.

**turnId stamped in:**
- \`api.ts\` \`/cc/say\`: \`onAssistantText\` (text segments), \`onToolEnd\` (tool events), final \`result.content\` write
- \`router.ts\`: \`onToolStart\` flush (text segments), \`onToolEnd\` (tool events), main response, thread response

**Graceful degradation:** messages predating the stamping or from dispatchers that don't set it (heartbeat, etc.) fall back to per-message bubbles — no schema migration needed.

## Bonus audit (not fixed in this PR — needs your call)

5 dispatchers use timestamps in their session keys, so each fire creates a fresh claude session (same anti-pattern as the v2.1.5 jack-key bug). High-value to unify into the agent's main \`jack:<slug>\` thread:
- \`pulse-recovery:<ts>\`, \`pulse-escalation:<ts>\`, \`herald-narration:<ts>\`, \`failsafe-heartbeat:<ts>\`, \`agent:<...>:channel-<id>-<msgid>\`

Pinged in the last reply for the call on which to unify.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm build\` / \`pnpm type-check\` clean
- [x] \`pnpm test\` 559/559 (no new tests — TUI rendering is React, existing infra is data-layer; graceful-degradation property covers the failure mode)
- [ ] Manual: trigger a multi-tool claude response, verify it renders as one bubble with header + text + tool rows + text inline, not N timestamped chunks

body:
## Summary

**Second external audit finding** on the BUG-PROD-004-FU1 cycle. After PR #130 fixed the RETRY ticket file (audit #1), the reviewer flagged that \`product-tracker.md\` Active Session panel was still stale — same class of failure as audit #1, on a sibling surface.

### Stale state (before this PR)

- **Line 11** \`**Last Updated:** 2026-04-15 (BUG-PROD-004-FU1-RETRY in progress)\`
- **Line 13** \`**Active Feature:** BUG-PROD-004-FU1-RETRY — Step 5/6 (Review)\`
- **Line 14** \`**Last Completed:** BUG-PROD-004-FU1-REVERT\` (should be bumped to FU1-RETRY)

A future session reading the tracker from the top would conclude a non-existent task is active. Same root cause as audit #1: **downstream documentation state does not follow upstream terminal state in split cycles unless explicitly synced**.

### Iteration-loop failure mode acknowledged

PR #130 was specifically about closing downstream state after the RETRY cycle closed — but I only addressed the ticket file, not the tracker panel. Audit #2 caught the sibling surface. The reviewer was right that this is ironic: the fix for audit #1 reproduced audit #1's root cause on a different surface.

## Changes

1. **\`docs/project_notes/product-tracker.md\` Active Session panel** fully re-synced:
   - \`Last Updated\` → "post BUG-PROD-004-FU1 full cycle close, 8 PRs total"
   - \`Active Feature\` → \`None\` with full cycle summary (PR history #123 → #130, final state, next candidates)
   - New \`Last Completed\` row for BUG-PROD-004-FU1-RETRY with merge commit \`0a9f5b6\`, PR #129 reference, and explicit note that PR #130 completed its Step 6 housekeeping after audit #1 and this PR completes the tracker panel sync after audit #2

2. **\`docs/project_notes/bugs.md\` preventive rule strengthened**: previously was only about ticket files. Now explicitly covers BOTH the ticket file AND the tracker Active Session panel as downstream state that must be synced together in every cycle close. Documents the iteration-loop failure mode. Adds a concrete verification command: \`git grep -n "Active Feature" docs/project_notes/product-tracker.md\` after every cycle close. Rule renamed accordingly.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`ci-success\` stays green (expected: path filter skips all test-* jobs because docs-only)
- [ ] Post-merge: tracker \`Active Feature\` line reads "None" with cycle summary, \`Last Updated\` line reflects the full cycle close
- [ ] Post-merge: running \`git grep -n "FU1-RETRY" docs/project_notes/product-tracker.md\` returns only the Last Completed entry, not the Active Feature line

## Summary
Fixed the AI response sanitization logic in `ai_client.py` to properly strip summary prefixes that include quotes, such as 'summary": "Hello..."'. 

The previous regex only handled cases like 'summary: ' but not 'summary": '. The updated regex now allows for optional quotes after the summary/response keywords and properly cleans the response.

## Changes
- Updated the regex pattern in `_parse_and_handle_response` method from `r'^(?:summary|Summary|response|Response):\s*'` to `r'^(?:summary|Summary|response|Response)"?\s*:\s*["\']*'`
- This ensures that malformed JSON fragments like 'summary": "text"' are properly sanitized to just 'text'

## Testing
Verified that the regex correctly handles various input formats:
- 'summary": "Hello world!"' → 'Hello world!'
- 'Summary: "How are you?"' → 'How are you?'
- 'response": Hello there' → 'Hello there'

Built for [reynerabdon13](https://strata-marketing.slack.com/archives/D0AKFKQGFEX/p1776252226279549?thread_ts=1776163570.435349&cid=D0AKFKQGFEX) by [Kilo for Slack](https://kilo.ai/features/slack-integration)

Problem: after signing, window.location.replace(sameURL) could return a cached version of the page (browser/CDN cache), making the page still show "en attente de signature" even though the DB was correctly updated to "signe".

Fixes:
- Replace window.location.replace(pathname) with router.refresh() which asks Next.js to re-render the server component with fresh DB data — no page reload needed, SignaturePage unmounts cleanly when statut becomes 'signe'
- Add fallback: window.location.href with ?t=timestamp after 3s in case router.refresh() is slow; timestamp busts any CDN/browser cache
- Cleanup fallback timer on component unmount (prevents double-navigation)
- Handle already_signed (idempotent case) separately with proper UX message and immediate refresh, instead of showing "Contrat signé avec succès!"

author: ahsanhabib9191
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) and missing authentication. The `delete_chat` and `update_name` endpoints for research chats were using `findByIdAndDelete` and `findByIdAndUpdate` based solely on the URL parameter ID, without verifying the current user's authentication or ensuring the user actually owned the chat. Additionally, the `update_name` endpoint was improperly mapped to `title` instead of the correct `name` field per the schema.
🎯 Impact: Any unauthenticated or authenticated user could arbitrarily delete or modify the name of *any* other user's research chats simply by guessing or knowing the chat's MongoDB ObjectId.
🔧 Fix: Imported `getAuthenticatedUser()`, added an authentication check (returning 401 if unauthenticated), and changed the database queries to `findOneAndDelete` and `findOneAndUpdate` bound to both `_id: id` and `userId: user._id || user.id`. Fixed the update payload to map correctly to the `name` field.
✅ Verification: Ran the test suite (pre-existing failures remain but no new ones introduced in this area). Verified the source code structure using `read_file` to confirm the secure implementation of user-scoped database mutations.

author: teal-bauer
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #37.

Installs the U-Boot side of the A/B watchdog. A `uboot_ab_check`
script in the U-Boot env increments `uboot_ab_bootcount` on each
boot while `uboot_upgrade=1`. When the count exceeds
`uboot_ab_bootlimit` (default 3), it calls
`mmc partconf ${mender_uboot_dev} ${uboot_altbootpart_ack} ${uboot_altbootpart} 0`
to revert `PARTITION_CONFIG`, then resets.

Userspace (update-service, see librescoot/update-service#16) sets
`uboot_upgrade=1` before flipping and clears it on a healthy boot.

## Changes

- `uboot-env-sync.sh`: new `set-prepend-if-missing` directive so
  `bootcmd` can be migrated idempotently without `set-if-matches`
  needing to know the exact old value
- `uboot-ab-watchdog.conf`: installs `uboot_ab_bootlimit=3`,
  `uboot_ab_bootcount=0`, `uboot_upgrade=0` via `set-if-missing`,
  installs the `uboot_ab_check` script, and prepends
  `run uboot_ab_check;` to `bootcmd`

No U-Boot source changes required. Everything runs through
`uboot-env-sync` at boot. `mender_uboot_dev` is already set per
machine by the Mender U-Boot integration (1 on MDB, 2 on DBC).

## Not covered here

- Hardware verification that `mmc partconf` behaves as expected on
  both boards with the 2017.03 NXP U-Boot fork
- U-Boot still has to reach the point of reading env and running
  `bootcmd`. A crash before that is a hard brick

Refs librescoot/librescoot#23

author: jd
body:
Replace `git push -f` with `git push --atomic` and per-ref
`--force-with-lease=ref:expected_sha` so that either all stack branches
update or none do.

For updated branches, the lease uses the SHA from the GitHub API
response, so the push is rejected if the remote branch moved since we
last read it — even without a prior `git fetch` of those refs.

For new branches, an empty expected value allows the create while still
participating in the atomic transaction.

author: dkijania
body:
## Summary

- Extracts common archive SQL queries into a shared `archive_health_queries` library, used by the archive healthcheck, `missing_blocks_auditor`, and archive metrics
- Adds `mina-archive-healthcheck`, a lightweight CLI for probing archive node health via PostgreSQL
- Subcommands: `db-ready`, `block-height`, `block-recency`, `missing-blocks`, `unparented-blocks`, `ready`, `wait`
- All commands support `--json` output for machine consumption
- Refactors `missing_blocks_auditor` and `archive/lib/metrics.ml` to use the shared query library

## Design

The archive healthcheck talks directly to PostgreSQL (no dependency on a running daemon or archive-node-api). Health signals:

| Check | What it queries |
|-------|----------------|
| `db-ready` | `SELECT MAX(height) FROM blocks` (connectivity test) |
| `block-recency` | Latest block timestamp vs wall clock |
| `missing-blocks` | Height gaps in sliding window |
| `unparented-blocks` | Blocks with no parent |
| `ready` | All of the above combined |
| `wait` | Polls `ready` until pass or timeout |

**Relationship to `missing-blocks-auditor`**: The auditor does deep integrity checks (recursive CTE chain walk, bitmask exit codes) for periodic audit + auto-repair via the guardian script. The healthcheck does fast, lightweight probes for k8s readiness/liveness. Both share SQL via `archive_health_queries`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI build passes
- [ ] Manual testing against archive database
- [ ] Verify `missing_blocks_auditor` still works after refactoring

author: paszkow
body:
The condition variable predicate for repair tasks unconditionally returned true (introduced in e5928497ce), which meant event.wait(pred) never actually suspended: do_until checks the predicate first, and if it's already satisfied, returns immediately without calling the inner wait(). This caused two problems:
1. The while(true) loop busy-spun, polling without blocking between topology changes.
2. During shutdown, event.broken() had no effect because no waiter was registered on the CV. The loop kept spinning, holding the HTTP server's task gate open and preventing http_server::stop() from completing. After ~15 minutes, systemd killed the process with SIGABRT.

The fix replaces the synchronous predicate with an async task_finished() helper that dispatches on the task type. Since the repair check is async (for_each_tablet scans every tablet), we cannot use event.wait(Pred). Instead, we register a waiter via event.wait() *before* running the async check, ensuring no broadcast is missed during the check. event.broken() during shutdown propagates broken_condition_variable to the registered waiter and unblocks the loop promptly.

Fixes: https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/SCYLLADB-1532

The commit that introduced a regression was backported to 2026.1. So this fix requires a backport as well.

author: neo23x0
body:
## Summary
- replace most source-side binary execution watches with generic process creation telemetry using `execve` / `execveat` on both `b32` and `b64`
- keep the ruleset focused on config / integrity changes and non-exec syscall semantics, while removing redundant per-binary exec tagging now better handled in Sigma / SIEM content
- fix malformed and incomplete audit rules, document the intended use of `-i`, and expand CI with linting plus host-aware Ubuntu load validation

## Rationale
- The original ruleset mixed telemetry collection with source-side detection logic. Once generic process execution telemetry exists, many `-w ... -p x`, `-F path=... -F perm=x`, and narrow exec subsets become redundant and increase maintenance cost without adding real coverage.
- This change intentionally makes execution collection dumber and broader: collect all process creation, then decide in Sigma / SIEM whether a given execution is interesting based on `exe`, `comm`, parent / child relationships, user context, TTY, arguments, network behavior, and surrounding events.
- Keeping binary-specific exec rules in the rules file creates path churn, distro variance, and frequent debates over what is or is not “suspicious” at collection time. Moving that classification downstream makes the audit ruleset lighter and easier to keep portable.
- Config / integrity rules are still kept where they add direct value: system configuration, service definitions, startup paths, shell profile locations, Docker state/config paths, CrowdStrike config paths, and the `/bin`, `/usr`, and `/boot` write telemetry.
- Non-exec syscall rules are also still kept where they provide semantics beyond generic process telemetry, such as module loading, mounts, time changes, ptrace, memfd creation, file permission changes, socket creation, and failed-access patterns.
- The repo keeps `-i` on purpose so optional distro-specific paths do not abort rule loading on systems where those files, directories, or users are absent. That keeps the default deployment simple, while the README explains how to validate a strict copy without `-i` before rollout.
- Several malformed or incomplete rules were fixed so the portable default is fail-open only for host-specific optional coverage, not because of syntax errors in the repo itself.
- CI is split into a static lint layer and a host-aware Ubuntu load-validation layer. The lint catches malformed rule patterns directly, while the load test verifies that the rules can be compiled and loaded on a real runner without clobbering host audit configuration.

## Testing
- `bash ./scripts/lint-rules.sh audit.rules`
- `bash -n scripts/lint-rules.sh scripts/validate-rules-ci.sh`
- GitHub Actions workflow added for audit rule validation

## Notes
- Full local `auditctl` / `augenrules` validation was not possible in this workspace because the audit tooling is not installed here.
- Multiple keys on a single rule are supported by `auditctl(8)`; however, after simplifying execution detection around `process_creation`, the ruleset now relies much less on source-side exec tagging overall.

## Summary

Implements the ISG Constitution v1 — a governance layer enforcing a 6-step fractal law (`تعيين → تصنيف → تحقق → استدعاء → فضّ → عبور/رد`) that every prior knowledge atom must pass before influencing interpretation. Sits upstream of Composition/Syntax Constitution v1.

## Changes

- **12 enums** in `core/enums.py`: `KnowledgeAtomType` (10), `PriorKnowledgeType` (10), `EpistemicEntryKind` (5), `ConfirmationRank` (5), `SourceType` (6), `LevelMatchStatus` (7), `CallabilityStatus` (3), `InternalConflictType` (6), `ISGConflictResolution` (7), `GateDecision` (4), `ReadinessLevel` (3), `VerificationStatus` (4)
- **7 frozen dataclasses** in `core/types.py`: `KnowledgeAtom`, `SourceRecord`, `LevelMatchResult`, `CallabilityResult`, `InternalConflictRecord`, `GovernanceGateResult`, `ISGValidationResult`

from arabic_engine.cognition.isg_v1 import identify_atom, govern

author: wesley-perkins-software
body:
## Summary

Two print CSS bugs in `src/styles/global.css` combined to force a spurious blank second page whenever a worksheet was printed:

- **`min-height: 100vh` on body** — Tailwind's `min-h-screen` (set in `BaseLayout.astro`) resolves to the browser viewport height (~270mm) in print context. With the `@media print` rule adding `margin: 14mm` top and bottom, the body box exceeded the 279mm letter page height, always producing a blank overflow page. Fixed by adding `min-height: 0 !important` inside `@media print`.

- **`space-y-6` phantom margin on `.worksheet-area`** — The `WorksheetGenerator` outer wrapper uses `space-y-6`, which applied `margin-top: 1.5rem (~8mm)` to `.worksheet-area` because its preceding `.no-print` sibling is `display:none` but lacks the HTML `hidden` attribute. Tailwind's `:not([hidden])` selector only strips the HTML attribute, not CSS `display:none`, so the phantom margin persisted in print. Fixed by adding `.worksheet-area { margin-top: 0 !important }` in `@media print`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Generate 20 standard division problems → Print Worksheet → print preview shows exactly 1 page, no blank 2nd page
- [ ] Generate 12 long division (With Remainders) problems → Print Worksheet → print preview shows exactly 1 page
- [ ] Verify the same fix applies to addition, subtraction, and multiplication worksheets (same `WorksheetGenerator` component)
- [ ] Confirm on-screen layout is unchanged (`min-h-screen` still applies outside `@media print`)

author: sagarbhandarii
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure a SecureWrapper is initialized early in the app lifecycle by injecting `SecureWrapper.ensureInit(context)` into startup methods so the security wrapper and native watchdog run before app code.
- Provide a reusable `wrapper-sdk` library that bridges to an external security SDK, performs hook/tamper checks, and exposes a native watchdog.
- Add a Gradle plugin to perform bytecode instrumentation at build time so initialization is injected automatically without changing application sources.

### Description
- Add a new Gradle plugin module `wrapper-inject-plugin` which registers `com.wrapper.inject` and uses the Android Instrumentation API plus ASM (`WrapperInjectPlugin`, `WrapperClassVisitorFactory`, `WrapperClassVisitor`, `WrapperMethodVisitor`) to inject a static call to `com.wrapper.sdk.SecureWrapper.ensureInit` into `Application.onCreate` and `Activity.onCreate` and configure frames computation.
- Add a new Android library module `wrapper-sdk` that contains `SecureWrapper`, `WrapperEngine`, `WrapperInitProvider` (ContentProvider auto-init), `Watchdog` (native library integration), `CoreSdkBridge`, `HookDetector`, and `TamperDetector`, plus JNI stub and CMake configuration.
- Update project configuration by adding the new modules in `settings.gradle.kts`, applying the plugin and adding the `:wrapper-sdk` dependency in `app/build.gradle.kts`, and wiring the plugin classpath in the app buildscript.
- Configure Kotlin/Java toolchains and dependencies (ASM, Android Gradle plugin compileOnly, placeholder `com.your.security:core-sdk:1.0.0`) for the new modules.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: agbaber
body:
## Summary

Clicking the checkmark on an already-selected answer card now clears the selection instead of being a no-op. Previously the only way to change state on a question was to pick a *different* answer — you couldn't return to an undecided state. That nudged residents toward committing to a view, which is at odds with the site's neutral stance, and also inflated the "My positions" count for users who only meant to browse (the first card tap auto-selects).

The `deselectAnswer` function was already defined in `index.html` but nothing called it — dead code. This wires it up and fills in the side effects it was missing.

## Changes

- **`.answer-check` click handler** (index.html:4928): toggles — if the card is already `.selected`, call `deselectAnswer(q)`; otherwise `selectAnswer(q, a)` as before.
- **`deselectAnswer`** (index.html:5491): now also hides the "next question" button, refreshes the stats strip, question social bar, and browse hint, updates checkmark tooltips, and fires an `explore_answer_deselected` PostHog event.
- **`updateAnswerCheckTitles()` helper** (index.html:5481): keeps each checkmark's tooltip in sync — "Make this my view" when unpicked, "Clear this view" when picked. Called from `selectAnswer`, `deselectAnswer`, `switchTopic`'s restore path, and the reset button handler.

The card body's click behavior is unchanged: first tap still selects + views, subsequent taps still browse evidence. Deselection is only available via the checkmark, so it's a deliberate action rather than something you can trigger by accidentally tapping a card you'd already committed to.

Server-side counters (`incrementSocial('q', ...)`, `submitVote`) are **not** rolled back on deselect — those are fire-and-forget and the "decided count" for the community stays sticky.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh session → tap a card → checkmark fills, evidence opens, next-question button appears
- [ ] Hover the filled checkmark → tooltip reads "Clear this view"
- [ ] Click the filled checkmark → selection clears, evidence closes, next-question button hides, progress dot for that topic un-lights, stats strip "decided" count decrements
- [ ] After deselect, tooltip on all three checkmarks reads "Make this my view"
- [ ] Notes pill count updates correctly on deselect; if it drops to 0, the pill hides and any open notes panel closes
- [ ] Deselect, then navigate back to landing → that topic's pip is cleared and `has-pick` is gone
- [ ] Deselect, then reload → selection stays cleared (localStorage persisted)
- [ ] Switching to a different answer still works as before (no extra deselect step required)
- [ ] URL `?q=override&pos=a` → deselect → URL becomes `?q=override` (history.replaceState, not a new entry)

Profiler unit tests were calling `os.environ["key"] = "value"` to change local behavior. But that changes the testing processes environment, polluting other tests.

author: shuv-amp
body:
# Summary

Fixes #3045

Stub and interface files can declare descriptor-backed attributes without showing the runtime initializer. Today we only apply descriptor semantics when the field is initialized in the class body, marked as `ClassVar`, or covered by a special case. That makes stub-declared descriptors fall back to their raw descriptor type instead of the `__get__` result.

This change treats fields modeled as `ClassFieldInitialization::Magic` as class-level for descriptor detection. That restores descriptor semantics for stub and interface declarations while preserving the current behavior for annotation-only instance attributes in source files.

The regression test covers an inherited annotation-only descriptor declared in `.pyi` files.

# Test Plan

- `python3 test.py --no-test --no-conformance --no-jsonschema`
- `cargo test -p pyrefly descriptors --quiet`
- `cargo test -p pyrefly test_foreign_key_basic --quiet`

author: joasisk
body:
### Motivation
- Provide an initial Phase 3 backend slice to support the "what should I do now" use case via a deterministic, rules-based daily planner.
- Capture explainable recommendation data (reasons and `score_breakdown`) and expose a placeholder for overload detection to enable later tuning and AI integration.
- Keep scope low-risk by relying on existing Phase 2 models so no DB migrations are required for this first implementation.

### Description
- Add a new planning route `GET /api/v1/planning/daily-plan` implemented in `apps/api/app/api/v1/phase3.py` and wire the router into the v1 API registration in `apps/api/app/api/v1/__init__.py`.
- Introduce Phase 3 Pydantic contracts in `apps/api/app/schemas/phase3.py` describing recommendations, `score_breakdown`, and overload placeholders (`overload_risk_level`, `drivers`, `recommended_reset_actions`).
- Implement a deterministic, rules-based scorer in `apps/api/app/services/phase3.py` that ranks visible non-terminal tasks using deadlines (hard/soft), priority/urgency, spouse influence, dependency readiness, and optional `current_energy`, with stable tie-breaking by `task_id`.
- Add tests in `apps/api/tests/test_phase3_daily_plan.py` covering hard-deadline prioritization, dependency readiness penalty, and deterministic ordering for identical input.

### Testing
- `python -m compileall app tests/test_phase3_daily_plan.py` was run and completed successfully (module compilation passed).
- `pytest -q tests/test_phase3_daily_plan.py tests/test_phase2_crud_flow.py` was executed but failed during test collection due to a missing test dependency (`httpx`) required by `fastapi.testclient`, causing the run to abort.
- The new modules were compiled and validated via `python -m compileall` but full test execution requires installing `httpx` in the test environment to run the `TestClient`-based suites.

author: hendricius
body:
Lets the Clawy CLI on each VM identify exactly which fork release the installed openclaw is from — the admin instance page will show e.g. \`clawy-2026.4.12-beta.1-1\` next to the version, instead of just \"fork build\".

## Workflow changes

- Run \`pnpm build\` + \`pnpm ui:build\` as explicit steps instead of letting \`pnpm pack\`'s prepack hook do it. We need to write into \`dist/\` *after* the build but *before* pack copies it into the tarball.
- Write \`dist/clawy-release.json\` with \`{ tag, commit, built_at }\`.
- Run \`pnpm pack\` with \`OPENCLAW_PREPACK_PREPARED=1\` so prepack skips the rebuild (which would wipe our marker) and just verifies the prepared dist/ — exactly the behavior the [prepack script](../blob/main/scripts/openclaw-prepack.ts) supports for this case.

\`dist/\` is already in \`package.json\`'s \`files\` list, so the marker rides along automatically.

## Effect

- **Fork tarball**: contains \`dist/clawy-release.json\`. CLI reads it, reports tag in metrics.
- **Upstream tarball**: no such file. CLI reports empty release tag → admin shows just \"upstream\" (no tag), unchanged behavior.

## Test plan

Merge → push next \`clawy-*\` tag → tarball contains the marker → check by:
\`\`\`
curl -sL https://github.com/Allonsygmbh/openclaw/releases/latest/download/openclaw.tgz | tar -tzf - | grep clawy-release
\`\`\`

author: hazimprojects
body:
### Motivation
- Recent background color changes were not appearing for users because browsers and the service worker were serving older cached CSS/JS/manifest assets.  
- The intent is to force clients to fetch fresh assets and rotate service-worker caches so the new styles take effect immediately.

### Description
- Updated service worker cache key from `hzedu-v11` to `hzedu-v12` and replaced precache entries to the versioned assets `'/assets/css/style.css?v=53'`, `'/assets/js/main.js?v=56'`, and `'/manifest.json?v=2'` in `sw.js`.
- Updated service worker registration to `sw.js?v=12` in `assets/js/main.js` so clients will install the new worker and trigger cache activation.
- Replaced asset query tokens across site pages to point to new versions, e.g. `style.css?v=53`, `main.js?v=56`, and added `?v=2` to manifest links (`/manifest.json?v=2`) in HTML files so browsers request fresh copies.
- Performed bulk edits to update all affected HTML files under the site (home, notes, quiz, and others) to keep references consistent with the service worker precache.

### Testing
- Ran targeted searches (`rg`) to confirm old tokens are absent and new tokens appear, which returned matches for the updated `style.css?v=53`, `main.js?v=56`, `sw.js?v=12`, `manifest.json?v=2`, and `hzedu-v12` entries and no matches for the previous tokens. (success)
- Inspected `sw.js` and `assets/js/main.js` to verify the `CACHE` value and registration URL changed to `hzedu-v12` and `sw.js?v=12` respectively. (success)
- Executed the automated replacement scripts used to update HTML files and verified modified files show the updated versioned asset URLs. (success)

author: umihyo24
body:
### Motivation
- Introduce full swap/replace mechanics for units including status interactions so switching can be planned, validated, and resolved in the turn simulation.
- Prevent unintended swaps while units are immobilized by a new "bind" debuff and ensure certain statuses are cleared or preserved correctly on swapping.

### Description
- Added a new `bind` status and per-unit switch flags (`isSwitching`, `switchTargetId`) and team `tileEffects` arrays in the initial state; introduced helpers `getStatusState`, `clearSwitchSensitiveStatuses`, and `clearSwitchFlags` to manage switch-related state.
- Implemented switch action collection and priority sorting inside `resolveTurn`, separated switch actions from other actions, validated switch targets and switch eligibility at resolution time, and cleared/retained statuses appropriately when swapping in `runSwitchAction` and `applySwitchResult`.
- Refactored target/pattern utilities (`getPatternPositionsForMove`, `isRuleMatchAtPosition`) and made `getValidTargetsForMoveInState` rely on a central rule matcher to simplify target validation.
- Updated planning and UI flow to support selecting reserves and confirming swaps by setting `actor.isSwitching`/`actor.switchTargetId`, preventing duplicate/reserved picks, disabling switch UI when bound, updating summary text and navigation messages, and clearing switch flags at end of playback.
- Adjusted event messages for switch actions and added support for `enterEffects` messages to be shown when a unit enters the battle.

### Testing
- Ran the existing automated test suite with `npm test` which completed successfully.
- Performed automated turn-resolution smoke checks by running the simulation step to verify switch actions are queued and resolved without runtime errors.

author: thatsmyboye
body:
The previous exact-string approach for Bug A (Readonly<{}> event types)
matched against a fixed multi-line literal that included the eslint-disable
comment.  Any variation in the published source — trailing whitespace,
CRLF vs LF, missing comment, or a slightly different comment format —
silently failed (logged "already patched") while leaving the Codegen-
crashing Readonly<{}> type in place.

Replace with a global RegExp that:
  • optionally strips the preceding eslint-disable[-next-line] comment
  • matches the type alias regardless of surrounding whitespace
  • handles with/without the `export` keyword in one pass

Also extend patchFile() to accept [RegExp, string] pairs alongside the
existing [string, string] pairs, using a before/after content comparison
to detect whether the regex actually matched anything.

Bug B (export type → type for CT.WithDefault string-union aliases) is
unchanged because exact matching is reliable for those short, stable lines.

body:
This change focuses on achieving a 100% Google PageSpeed Insights score on mobile by removing heavy third-party libraries (Swiper and AOS) and replacing them with custom, high-performance native implementations. 

Key changes:
1. **Custom Slider:** A new vanilla JS slider implementation using CSS `scroll-snap-type` for smooth, native-feeling scrolling. It supports pagination, navigation buttons, and smart autoplay (resets on interaction).
2. **Custom Animations:** An `IntersectionObserver` based animation system that replaces AOS. It uses the same `data-aos` style attributes (migrated to `data-aos-custom`) but without the overhead of the AOS library.
3. **PSI Optimizations:** 
    - Critical CSS updated to include new component styles.
    - Added `width`, `height`, and `fetchpriority` to the logo.
    - Guaranteed `display=swap` for all fonts.
    - Removed multiple external HTTP requests by eliminating library CDNs.
4. **Maintenance:** Removed all dead code related to the previous libraries and ensured no visual regressions were introduced.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
The SIM protection feature was not working correctly on modern Android devices because it relied on the implicit broadcast `android.intent.action.SIM_STATE_CHANGED`. Modern versions of Android (and OEM skins) restrict or delay these broadcasts, making them unreliable for critical immediate triggers. 

This fix removes the outdated `simStateReceiver` broadcast listener and replaces it with `SubscriptionManager.OnSubscriptionsChangedListener`. This explicitly tracks state changes in active SIM subscriptions, and queries `TelephonyManager.simState` locally to correctly identify whether a SIM has been removed. This approach provides a reliable and compliant method to trigger the anti-theft functionality.

author: marcporciuncula
body:
## Summary

- Adds `avm-bridge editor open <path>` command that opens files in the user's host editor (Cursor/VS Code) via remote-SSH, connected to the requesting container
- Daemon resolves container identity from the auth token to build the correct SSH remote target — a container cannot open files "as" another container
- Validates editor binary exists and SSH config is installed before launching, returning actionable errors to the agent

## Why

When a user asks the in-avm agent to "open this file in my editor," the agent previously had no way to do it. The editor is on the host, not inside the container. This bridges that gap using the daemon infrastructure from #20.

## Test plan

- Build and verify `avm-bridge editor open --help` shows correct args
- Create a container, run `avm-bridge editor open /home/agent/.bashrc` from inside — editor opens on host connected via SSH to the container
- Verify missing SSH config returns a `FailedPrecondition` error with actionable guidance

author: zaitonzz
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive set of features and improvements centered around enhanced user management for administrators, stricter account status enforcement, and improved security for user authentication. The main changes include a new admin user management controller, middleware for enforcing active status and mandatory password changes, user model enhancements, and updates to authentication flows.

**Key changes:**

### Admin User Management

* Added `AdminUserManagementController` for full CRUD operations on users, including role and status management, doctor profile syncing, and guardrails to prevent admins from demoting or deactivating themselves. Sends temporary credentials via email on user creation. (`app/Http/Controllers/AdminUserManagementController.php`)
* Introduced `StoreAdminUserRequest` and `UpdateAdminUserRequest` for robust validation of admin user creation and updates, including conditional validation for doctor profiles. (`app/Http/Requests/StoreAdminUserRequest.php`, `app/Http/Requests/UpdateAdminUserRequest.php`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ad9c3e936f7bd0f962f84dae1aa546bac5acb1f6774a80c6afb87f42e1a9359dR1-R52) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bf03bca000cf182247deb9e92f443b55d919c0f836cc95ac46d95006ac458facR1-R56)
* Added `AdminUserTemporaryPasswordMail` for sending new users their temporary credentials. (`app/Mail/AdminUserTemporaryPasswordMail.php`)

### User Model Enhancements

* Extended `User` model with `status` and `must_change_password` attributes, and helper methods: `isActive()`, `isInactive()`, `isSuspended()`, and `requiresPasswordChange()`. (`app/Models/User.php`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-37a2d7d879a7de3f7d73b2975cd22be9f41ec10c334a0dda9ad1e869332e4ecbR28-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-37a2d7d879a7de3f7d73b2975cd22be9f41ec10c334a0dda9ad1e869332e4ecbR62) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-37a2d7d879a7de3f7d73b2975cd22be9f41ec10c334a0dda9ad1e869332e4ecbR92-R111)

### Middleware for Account Status and Security

* Added `EnsureActiveUserStatus` middleware to log out and block access for suspended/inactive users, with appropriate messaging and JSON/redirect responses. (`app/Http/Middleware/EnsureActiveUserStatus.php`)
* Added `EnsurePasswordChangeRequired` middleware to force users with the `must_change_password` flag to update their password before proceeding. (`app/Http/Middleware/EnsurePasswordChangeRequired.php`)
* Registered the new middleware in the application and attached them to the web middleware stack. (`bootstrap/app.php`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-10bc2462d34ebc59a5d482a1faca04ce74f6df89fcc2ef8bfb17b939647ea518R3-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-10bc2462d34ebc59a5d482a1faca04ce74f6df89fcc2ef8bfb17b939647ea518R42-R50)

### Authentication and OTP Flow Improvements

* Updated OTP and login flows to check for active status before allowing authentication, and to route users who must change their password directly to the password change page. (`app/Http/Controllers/OtpVerificationController.php`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-013b65a27e37f9a2a187e3725cddbe28ec24bda3223830b75c33e49525415b0cR6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-013b65a27e37f9a2a187e3725cddbe28ec24bda3223830b75c33e49525415b0cL75-R76) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-013b65a27e37f9a2a187e3725cddbe28ec24bda3223830b75c33e49525415b0cR85-R95) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-013b65a27e37f9a2a187e3725cddbe28ec24bda3223830b75c33e49525415b0cL319-R323) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-013b65a27e37f9a2a187e3725cddbe28ec24bda3223830b75c33e49525415b0cL335-R341) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-013b65a27e37f9a2a187e3725cddbe28ec24bda3223830b75c33e49525415b0cR509-R538)
* On password update, the `must_change_password` flag is cleared. (`app/Http/Controllers/Settings/PasswordController.php`)

These changes collectively provide robust administrative user management, enforce account status and password policies, and improve security and user experience across authentication flows.

author: mabry1985
body:
## Summary

Two fixes discovered during end-to-end Quinn testing via Ava.

### 1. Streaming early-break (closes feature-1776309307266)

\`A2AExecutor._executeStream\` held the SSE connection open after receiving a non-terminal \`task\` event, waiting for more stream events. Quinn (and agents like her) use the stream transport only for the initial \`submitted\` event, then do the work in the background. Holding the stream open for 2+ minutes until the sync caller times out was crashing her SSE generator with \`GeneratorExit\` (visible in Quinn's logs on every long-running task).

**Fix**: on non-terminal task events, break out of the SSE loop and let TaskTracker drive the task to completion via polling / resubscribe. Terminal states still flow through the stream end-to-end.

### 2. Push-callback URL routing (closes feature-1776309298112)

\`WORKSTACEAN_BASE_URL\` is set to \`http://ava:8081\` (the host's Tailscale MagicDNS name) so protoPen — running externally on steamdeck — can reach the callback. But internal docker agents resolve \`ava\` to their own 127.0.1.1, so the callback URL is unreachable from inside the shared docker network.

**Fix**: \`SkillDispatcherPlugin._pickCallbackBaseUrl\` inspects the target agent's URL. Single-label hostnames (docker service names like \`http://quinn:7870\`) get \`WORKSTACEAN_INTERNAL_BASE_URL\` (default \`http://workstacean:3000\`). FQDN/IP hosts get the existing \`WORKSTACEAN_BASE_URL\`.

Exposes \`A2AExecutor.url\` as a public getter so the dispatcher can see the agent URL without piercing config.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bun test\` — 946 pass / 0 fail
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Post-deploy: Ava dispatches to Quinn, verify no \`GeneratorExit\` in Quinn's logs
- [ ] Post-deploy: verify push-notification callback URL is \`http://workstacean:3000/api/a2a/callback/...\` for Quinn

author: artemgetmann
body:
## Review Fast Path

- User path fixed: consumer app launch at login by default, but normal Quit now stays quit for the rest of the current login session.
- Proof: packaged consumer app smoke test passed; after Quit, the app stayed down for 60s while the gateway stayed running.
- Shared-state footgun removed: the app LaunchAgent is now detached from launchd on quit instead of relying on KeepAlive to stop relaunch loops.
- Still hurts: the separate verifier-script bundle-ID mismatch in this worktree lane is untouched.

## Why This Matters

- Normal Quit previously let launchd bring the app back, which made the consumer app feel broken and uncontrollable.
- This keeps the login-at-login behavior intact without turning Quit into a fake quit.

## Scope Boundary

- Changed only the macOS app quit path and app LaunchAgent helper.
- Did not touch the gateway/runtime shutdown path.
- Did not change the separate verifier-script lane.

## Verification

- Live-tested against `dist/OpenClaw Consumer.app`.
- Confirmed the app LaunchAgent stayed armed for next login.
- Confirmed the app did not relaunch after normal Quit.
- Confirmed the gateway kept running.

## AI Assistance

- AI-assisted
- testing degree: live-tested

author: copilot
body: Adds two runnable scripts that let anyone reproduce a demo checkpoint and a visual Before/After gallery in one command, plus the README scaffolding to present those results. ## New scripts ### `scripts/train_quick_demo.py` - 500 PSNR-pretraining + 300 GAN fine-tuning iterations; configurable via module-level constants - Reuses `src.train` helpers (`build_generator`, `build_discriminator`, `save_checkpoint`) — fully backward-compatible with existing configs - Writes TensorBoard scalars to `runs/esrgan_demo/` (skips gracefully if `tensorboard` absent) - Saves final checkpoint to `checkpoints/esrgan_demo_4x.pth` - Runnable as `python scripts/train_quick_demo.py` or `python -m scripts.train_quick_demo` ### `scripts/generate_results_gallery.py` - Loads demo checkpoint + `configs/inference_config.yaml`; both overridable via CLI - Selects up to 6 images from `data/sample/`; downloads 4 public-domain fallback images if empty - Runs tiled inference via `src.inference.run_inference`; simulates LR via bicubic downsampling - Outputs labelled side-by-side composites (LR bicubic | ESRGAN SR | HR) to `results/gallery/` - Computes PSNR + SSIM (via `src.utils`); LPIPS is optional (`pip install lpips`), emits `N/A` otherwise - Font resolution is cross-platform (Linux/macOS/Windows paths with Pillow fallback) - Writes `results/gallery_readme.md` — paste-ready Markdown table + `` gallery block **One-liner to reproduce:** ```bash python scripts/train_quick_demo.py && python scripts/generate_results_gallery.py ``` ## README - Top-of-file badges: Python 1.13+, PyTorch 1.13+, CI status, MIT, Hugging Face placeholder - New `## Results` section: placeholder metric table, Before/After `` gallery, highlight text, reproduction command - Fixed `## Example Outputs` placeholder text ## .gitignore Added `checkpoints/`, `runs/`, `results/` — all generated by the above scripts. ## Caveats - Metrics are self-referential (LR is bicubic-downsampled from the same HR), reflecting pipeline round-trip quality rather than real test-set performance - 500+300 iterations demonstrates the pipeline; meaningful SR quality requires full training with `--no-debug`

author: sentacraft
body:
## Summary

- Remove `bg-background` from the layout wrapper div so the body's `stone-100` shows through the `pb-safe-area-inset-bottom` padding zone
- The layout wrapper's bottom padding (home indicator zone) now always shows `stone-100` regardless of whether page content fills the screen
- Pages that need a white canvas declare `bg-background` on their own root element: browse, compare, detail, about

## Root Cause

In iOS PWA standalone mode, `100svh` may not equal the physical screen height, so short/non-scrolling pages (homepage, about) don't fill all the way to the bottom. The wrapper's white `bg-background` was leaking into the 34px home indicator zone, showing a white bar at the bottom.

## Test plan

- [ ] iOS PWA (Chrome or Safari "Add to Home Screen") — no white bar at bottom on any page
- [ ] Homepage: stone-100 background fills seamlessly to bottom
- [ ] About page (short content, non-scrolling on large screens) — no white bar
- [ ] Browse/Compare/Detail pages: white content renders correctly

author: shaobai-li
body:
## 概述
在发现各 Agent 可用 `SKILL.md` 的 YAML 头（`name`、`description`）及文件路径后，序列化为 `<skills>...</skills>` XML，并在调用模型前**动态拼接到 system 消息最前**，使模型在静态 `system.md` 之外仍能获知当前技能目录；`StandardAgent` 与 `WriteAgent` 通过 `get_system_prompt_for_llm()` 使用该组合后的系统提示。

## 改动说明
- 扩展 `skill_loader`：`SkillHead`、`discover_skills_for_agent`、`format_skills_discovery_xml`、`prepend_skill_catalog_xml_to_system_prompt`；仓库内技能根目录 `app/agents/skills/<skill_id>/`，用户技能在 `DATA_DIR` 下各 agent 的 `skills/`；合并规则与 `config.yaml` 中 `agents.<id>.skills` 一致。
- 新增 `BaseAgent.get_system_prompt_for_llm()`，在静态 `system_prompt` 前附加技能目录 XML。
- 调整 `StandardAgent._build_loop_messages`、`WriteAgent.handle_chat_stream`：发往 LLM 的 system 使用 `get_system_prompt_for_llm()`（再加标准 Agent 的工具说明 `guard`）。
- 修复 `app/core/config.py` 中 `config.yaml` 路径为相对 `config.py` 解析，避免工作目录不在 `backend` 时读不到配置导致技能列表为空。
- `prepend_skill_catalog_xml_to_system_prompt` 内增加 `[skill_catalog]` 控制台调试输出（ heads 数量、路径、XML 预览、合并长度），便于验证注入是否生效。

## 实现目的
- 将技能「发现层」与「完整 SKILL 正文加载」分离，控制首包上下文体积。
- 让模型在 system 中显式看到可用技能元数据与 `SKILL.md` 路径，便于按需对齐行为或配合工具读文件。
- 统一多 Agent 注入方式，后续可改为 logging 或关闭调试输出而不改调用链。

author: alxnko
body:
⚡ Bolt: optimize socket.io emit loop using batch broadcasting

Replaced inefficient loops that emitted messages to individual rooms with a single batch emit using an array of rooms in `meowsenger/pages/api/socket.ts`. This pattern leverages Socket.io's internal handling for multi-room broadcasting, significantly improving performance by reducing redundant broadcast logic and packet emissions.

### 💡 What:
The optimization replaces:
```typescript
participants.forEach((p) => {
  io.to(`user_${p.userId}`).emit("event", data);
});
```
with:
```typescript
const rooms = participants.map((p) => `user_${p.userId}`);
io.to(rooms).emit("event", data);
```

### 🎯 Why:
Socket.IO (v4+) allows broadcasting to an array of rooms in a single call. Looping over rooms and calling `emit` for each one is inefficient as it triggers the entire emission logic (including adapter communication) once per room. Batching these into a single `io.to(rooms).emit()` call allows Socket.IO to handle the broadcast more efficiently.

### 📊 Measured Improvement:
Using a mock benchmark script (`meowsenger/benchmarks/socket_emit_benchmark.js`):
- **Baseline (Loop):** ~259.68ms (1000 users, 100 repetitions)
- **Optimized (Batch):** ~33.94ms (1000 users, 100 repetitions)
- **Improvement:** ~7.6x faster in the simulated environment.

Tested logic with a standalone verification script `meowsenger/tests/socket_batch_verification.test.ts`.

Used the `URL` constructor for robust origin and path-prefix validation, ensuring that bypasses involving host-manipulation or sibling paths are blocked. - **[Backend-Worker/src/src-tests/schemas.spec.ts]:** Added comprehensive SSRF validation tests.

body:
## Summary

Full security and code quality review across all 8 areas of the codebase, with every issue found fixed.

### Critical fixes
- **SQL injection** in `risk_scorer.py` and `network.py` — parameterized DuckDB queries
- **Path traversal** in `backup.py` restore endpoint — strict backup_id allowlist
- **Stripe webhook blocked** by session auth — unblocked, secured by HMAC signature instead
- **AuthProvider never mounted** — `useAuth()` would crash on any page using it

### High severity
- **Timing attack** on password comparison → `hmac.compare_digest` + dummy salt
- **Rate limiter broken on Cloud Run** — all users shared one bucket (proxy IP); fixed with X-Forwarded-For last-hop
- **Session expiry bug** — claimed 30 days but enforced 1 day
- **Admin password fallback** was hardcoded `admin123`; now `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)`
- **Thread safety** on store, review_store, alert_store, audit_log, ml_scorer, supervised_scorer
- **Viewers could trigger scans/ML training** — now requires analyst role minimum
- **handleRegister** stored wrong session shape — user forced to re-login after every registration
- **downloadEvidence** bypassed auth headers

### Medium/Low severity
- Dockerfile runs as non-root user
- `.gitignore` covers users.json, sessions.json, private keys
- CSP header added to firebase.json
- HSTS header on HTTPS responses
- Unbounded query limits capped
- NPI validation on all 14 provider sub-routes
- Signal name allowlist on evidence endpoint
- Username validation on self-registration
- State code validation across multiple routes
- GCS sync list expanded with missing data files

## Test plan
- [ ] Login works, session persists 30 days
- [ ] Viewer cannot start scan or ML training (403)
- [ ] /metrics requires admin
- [ ] Watchlist and review queue persist across restarts

body:
### Motivation

- Standardize and modularize the ADA monitoring package by introducing an `mlp` namespace and separating workspace-level sources from product-level aggregators.  
- Reduce duplication and hardcoded workspace references inside domain functions to make domains consume stable product-level interfaces.  
- Add NOT PII and SIROSAG domains/helpers and update Grafana wrappers to reflect the refactor.  

### Description

- Renamed and migrated domain and helper functions from `fn_prd_ada_*` to `fn_prd_mlp_ada_*` and created new domain, helper and source functions for NOTPII and SIROSAG (for example `fn_prd_mlp_notpii_*` and `fn_prd_mlp_ssag_*`).  
- Introduced workspace-level source adapters `fn_src_mlp_ws_*` and product-level aggregators `fn_src_mlp_*` (e.g. `fn_src_mlp_ws_ada_table`, `fn_src_mlp_pipeline_runs_all`, `fn_src_mlp_systemlogs_all`) and replaced direct workspace `workspace(...)` calls inside domains with these adapters.  
- Added/updated ADA helpers to improve lag detection and KPI evaluation (`fn_prd_mlp_ada_alert_from_tables_lag`, `fn_prd_mlp_ada_alert_from_dispatch_nrt_logs`, `fn_prd_mlp_ada_kpi_alert_rows`) and created NOTPII helpers (`fn_prd_mlp_notpii_autoloader_alert`, `fn_prd_mlp_notpii_ingesta_job04_alert`) and SIROSAG helpers (`fn_prd_mlp_ssag_eval_*`).  
- Replaced or created Grafana wrappers to call the new domain names (examples: `grafana_wrappers/var_mlp_ada_dispatch.kql` now calls `fn_prd_mlp_ada_dom_dispatch_status`, and new wrappers `var_mlp_notpii_*` and `var_mlp_sirosag_resumen.kql` were added).  
- Deleted legacy files that used old names and moved/created `law_functions_body_only/` mirrors for body-only LAW UI convenience, and expanded documentation in `README.md` and `INVENTORY.md` to reflect the active graph.  
- Updated `validate_kql_references.py` to expect the new `mlp` naming, include the new required domains/helpers/wrappers, enforce a naming guardrail for source filenames (`fn_src_mlp_*`), and to validate that wrappers call exactly one domain function.  

### Testing

- Ran the package audit script `python3 refactor_ada_optimized/validate_kql_references.py` to verify definitions, wrapper presence and references, and naming guardrails, and it completed without errors.  
- Static validation found and prevented undefined calls and non-MLP source filenames by raising errors during the audit, which were addressed in this change set.  
- No runtime unit tests were added; changes were limited to KQL function renames, composition, and linter/validation updates.

author: shenxingy
body:
## Summary
Implements Appel Ch.10 (Liveness) + Ch.11 (Register Allocation) on top of Phase 5 instruction selection.

- **Liveness**: standard fixed-point dataflow with set-based equality so iteration terminates.
- **Color**: Chaitin/George-Appel graph coloring — simplify low-degree nodes onto a stack, potentialSpill highest-degree when stuck, select pops the stack and assigns colors.
- **RegAlloc**: outer driver builds CFG → liveness → interference → Color; if Color reports spills, `rewriteProgram` inserts lw/sw around uses and we recurse.
- **MipsFrame**: full register set (\$v0-\$v1, \$a0-\$a3, \$t0-\$t9, \$s0-\$s7) + tempMap precoloring; procEntryExit2 sink instruction so callee-saves stay live across the function.
- Bug fix: \`flowgraph.sml\` defined \`process()\` but never called it, leaving def/use tables empty (caught by spilled-temp test).

author: copilot
body:
Raw ETCS register values (0–255) were stored directly into speed fields without conversion, causing overspeed detection and all downstream consumers (DTC events, UDP/DMI frames) to operate on values ~5.5× too small compared to km/h.

## Changes

- **`bsw/kavach/src/KavachSensor.cpp`**: Added `readSpeedReg` helper lambda encapsulating the ETCS→km/h formula `(raw * 18) / 100`, applied to all four speed registers (`speedActual`, `speedPermitted`, `speedWarning`, `sectionSpeed`). Non-speed registers are unchanged.

```cpp
// Before
d.speedActual    = readReg(273);
d.speedPermitted = readReg(266);

// After
auto readSpeedReg = [&](uint16_t addr) { return (readReg(addr) * 18) / 100; };
d.speedActual    = readSpeedReg(273);
d.speedPermitted = readSpeedReg(266);
d.speedWarning   = readSpeedReg(275);
d.sectionSpeed   = readSpeedReg(365);
```

The overspeed predicate on line 48 (`speedActual > speedPermitted`) required no change — it was correct in structure but was consuming wrong-unit inputs.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Critical Bug: ETCS Speed Conversion Missing

The sensor reading function in `KavachSensor::readAll()` reads raw ETCS register values but never converts them to km/h. This causes overspeed detection to compare incompatible units.

### Current Behavior (WRONG)
```cpp
d.speedActual = readReg(273);       // raw ETCS units (0-255)
d.speedPermitted = readReg(266);    // raw ETCS units (0-255)
d.speedWarning = readReg(275);      // raw ETCS units (0-255)
d.sectionSpeed = readReg(365);      // raw ETCS units (0-255)
d.overspeed = (d.speedActual > d.speedPermitted && d.speedPermitted > 0);
```

The overspeed comparison on line 48 is comparing raw values, not km/h, causing a ~5.5x scale mismatch.

### Required Fix
According to SMOCIP specifications and your own documentation:
- Conversion formula: `(raw_value * 18) / 100 = km/h`

All speed register reads must apply this conversion immediately after reading from Modbus.

### Impact
- Overspeed detection currently uses wrong units
- DTC events log incorrect speed values
- Thresholds and fault logic are all off by ~5.5x
- Communication with ETCS (DMI via UDP) sends wrong speed values

### Solution
Apply the conversion formula to all speed register reads:
```cpp
d.speedActual = (readReg(273) * 18) / 100;      // convert to km/h
d.speedPermitted = (readReg(266) * 18) / 100;   // convert to km/h
d.speedWarning = (readReg(275) * 18) / 100;     // convert to km/h
d.sectionSpeed = (readReg(365) * 18) / 100;     // convert to km/h
```

This is a single-line fix per speed value that corrects all speed readings instantly.

User: Now I have the full picture of your DEM/DCM project. Let me do the comparison analysis:Look for gaps and SMOCIP referencesLook for gaps and SMOCIP referencesHere is the full gap analysis between your DEM/DCM and what SMOCIP-level production diagnostics require:

AreaStatus8 fault conditions with debounce✅UDS status byte (0x2F) with 5 bits✅DTC generation + NVM persistence✅CSV logging (4 files + 8 per-event)✅Live Modbus TCP sensor reading✅UDP to DMI (port 5600, 20-byte frame)✅DCM: 0x10, 0x14, 0x19, 0x22, 0x27✅DCM: 0x11, 0x2E, 0x31, 0x3E, 0x85✅Session control + security access✅RBI history across runs✅

What's Missing ❌ (Compared to SMOCIP)
1. ETCS Speed Conversion — Critical Bug
Your sensor reads raw register values but never converts them to km/h:
cpp// What you have (WRONG):
d.speedActual = blk[273 - 240];  // raw ETCS units

// What SMOCIP expects (CORRECT):
d.speedActual = (blk[273 - 240] * 18) / 100;  // km/h
Your doc says raw * 18/100 = km/h but the code doesn't do it. Fix this immediately — it means your overspeed detection is comparing wrong units.
2. Freeze Frame Data — Missing Entirely
SMOCIP stores sensor values at the moment of fault — not just that a fault occurred. When Over_Speeding triggers, freeze frame captures speed, signal, mode at that instant.
Add to EventMemoryEntry:
cppstruct FreezeFrame {
    uint16_t speedActual;
    uint16_t speedPermitted;
    uint8_t  signalAspect;
    uint8_t  kavachMode;
    uint32_t timestamp_ms;
};
And expose via DCM 0x19/0x04 (ReportDTCSnapshotRecord).
3. DTC Aging Counter — Incomplete
Your NVM stores agingCounter but nothing increments it. In AUTOSAR DEM, aging works like this:

Every time a passed test cycle occurs WITHOUT the fault, aging counter increments
When aging reaches threshold (e.g. 40 cycles) → DTC is auto-cleared
Currently your DTCs never age out — they persist forever

4. 0x19/0x06 Extended Data is Shallow
You return occ + aging but SMOCIP returns full extended data record:
DTC + UDS byte + occurrence count + aging counter + 
timestamp of first occurrence + timestamp of last occurrence + 
freeze frame sensor values

Your code currently just prints a warning and skips. These should be real DTCs.
6. 0x19/0x0A — ReportSupportedDTC — Missing
SMOCIP responds to 0x0A subfunction which lists all DTCs the ECU can ever produce (not just active ones). Diagnostic tools always query this first.
7. Full Supervision Mode (0x0002) Not Detected
Your event map includes KAVACH_EVT_MODE_FS 0x0002 but KavachConditions only detects MODE_TRIP (0x07). Full Supervision mode should also trigger an event.

author: is-primary-dev
body:
## Summary

Upstream commit 2f57090adb ("ini: Implement a new ini-file parser and adapt the code to use it") ported halui.cc's `HOME_SEQUENCE` check from the old `inifile.Find()` API to the new `inifile.isSet()` API and accidentally flipped the polarity of the condition that gates `halui.home-all` pin creation.

Originally from commit 38d35cdf8e ("Add pin home-all to halui pin is created only if HOME_SEQUENCE is properly defined in inifile"):

    if (inifile.Find("HOME_SEQUENCE", "JOINT_0")) {
        have_home_all = 1;
    }

`Find()` returned truthy when the key was defined, so the pin was created *when* `HOME_SEQUENCE` was properly set — matching the commit message's stated intent.

After 2f57090adb:

    if (!inifile.isSet("HOME_SEQUENCE", "JOINT_0")) {
        have_home_all = 1;
    }

`isSet()` returns true when the key is set, so with the added `!` the condition fires only when `HOME_SEQUENCE` is NOT set — the opposite of the original semantics.

## Observable symptom

Properly-configured machines (which define `HOME_SEQUENCE` in `[JOINT_0]`) no longer get the `halui.home-all` convenience pin:

    $ halcmd setp halui.home-all 1
    <commandline>:0: parameter or pin 'halui.home-all' not found

This affects any GUI, HAL script, or test harness that triggers home-all via this pin.

## Fix

Remove the `!`. Added a comment documenting the regression and the original semantics from 38d35cdf8e.

## Testing

Built against upstream master and verified on a simulation configuration with `[JOINT_0] HOME_SEQUENCE = 0`. Before the fix: `halcmd show pin halui.home-all` returns nothing. After the fix: the pin exists, and pulsing it correctly triggers home-all.

### Motivation
- The tutorial flow could start the next train wave immediately after accepting/rejecting, which could interrupt the off-screen movement and leave the accepted tutorial train stuck on screen.
- Wave progression needs to wait until any decided trains finish their movement so departure animations are not canceled.

### Description
- Added a `pendingWaveAdvanceCoroutine` field to track a queued wave-advance coroutine and avoid overlapping advances.

- The queued coroutine is stopped if a new decision occurs and cleared when it finishes.

author: maxjiang216
body:
## What went wrong (two bugs, same root cause chain)

### Bug 1 — WASM crash: `RuntimeError: function signature mismatch`

Allegro 5 falls back to **stb_image** when no external image codec (libpng/libjpeg) is available in the build. stb_image registers its load handlers via function pointers, but those pointers end up in Allegro's codec table with an incompatible type signature for WASM's `call_indirect` instruction → trap on first `al_load_bitmap()` call.

This is why the JPEG approach in the previous PR crashed: it wasn't a missing JPEG decoder per se, but stb_image being WASM-unsafe regardless of format.

### Bug 2 — Vercel 100 MB limit

156 MB of uncompressed BMPs. LZ4 only gave ~10% compression on this art (photographic gradients, anti-aliasing), leaving ~140 MB — still over the limit.

## Fix

**PNG via libpng** solves both:

- libpng registers a proper WASM-compatible function pointer → no crash
- PNG is lossless but ~4–6× smaller than BMP for anime-style art → ~30–45 MB total

### `deploy.yml`
- `embuilder build libpng` before cmake (populates emsdk sysroot)
- `-sUSE_LIBPNG=1` added to Allegro cmake `C_FLAGS`/`CXX_FLAGS` so `find_package(PNG)` succeeds and the PNG codec is compiled into `liballegro_monolith.a`
- Cache key bumped (`v6` → `v7-libpng`) to force Allegro rebuild

### `build-web.sh`
- Copy `assets/` → `web-assets/`, convert `*.bmp` → `*.png`, delete original BMPs
- Manifest generated with `--ext png`
- `file_packager.py` packages `web-assets/` (no `--lz4` needed; PNG is already compressed)
- `emcc` gets `-sUSE_LIBPNG=1` at link time
- `trap` cleans up `web-assets/` on exit

## Expected outcome
- CI build succeeds (Allegro compiled with libpng)
- `index.data` ~35–50 MB (under Vercel's 100 MB limit)
- Flipping cards works correctly in the deployed page

💡 What: Added caching via `window.expressionCache = new Map()` for `new Function(...)` calls used to evaluate math expressions in animation loops.
🎯 Why: Creating a `new Function` string dynamically on every tick of an animation loop (like `masterTimeline.time()`) forces the JavaScript engine into severe, continuous JIT compilation overhead.
📊 Impact: Expected ~30x performance improvement in expression execution based on local benchmarks (from 330ms to 10ms over 100k iterations). Reduces main-thread blocking and frame drops.
🔬 Measurement: Can be verified using performance timeline while scrubbing or playing animations where shapes use data-expr logic. Test via Node benchmark using `performance.now()`.

## Summary

- Adds a full self-update system to gwt (SPEC-2041): GitHub Releases check, binary self-replacement, installer dispatch (DMG/MSI/portable tar.gz), and restart.
- Startup auto-check runs 3 s after launch with 3 retries; on `Available` it broadcasts a toast notification to the WebView UI. CLI users can run `gwt update` for an explicit Y/N check-and-apply flow.
- Matches the UX of the former Tauri-era GUI installer: startup toast, confirm dialog, platform-native installer dispatch (hdiutil+ditto on macOS, msiexec on Windows), and post-exit restart.

## Changes

- `crates/gwt-core/src/update.rs` (new): `UpdateManager` — GitHub Releases API check with 24 h TTL cache, binary download, sha-less size validation, tar.gz/zip/dmg/msi/pkg extraction/dispatch, `internal_apply_update` (post-exit binary swap), `internal_run_installer` (post-exit installer launch), `is_ci()`, `make_helper_copy`, `write_restart_args_file`.
- `crates/gwt-core/src/paths.rs`: added `gwt_update_cache_path()` and `gwt_updates_dir()`.
- `crates/gwt-core/Cargo.toml`: enabled `reqwest`, `flate2`, `tar`, `zip`, `semver` workspace dependencies.
- `crates/gwt/src/cli/update.rs` (new): `gwt update [--check]` manual command and `gwt __internal apply-update / run-installer` subprocess helpers.
- `crates/gwt/src/cli.rs` + `cli/env.rs`: routed `update` and `__internal` subcommands.
- `crates/gwt/src/protocol.rs`: added `BackendEvent::UpdateState(gwt_core::update::UpdateState)` and `FrontendEvent::ApplyUpdate`.
- `crates/gwt/src/main.rs`: startup Tokio task (3 s delay, 3 retries, broadcasts `UpdateState` to WebSocket clients); `FrontendEvent::ApplyUpdate` handler spawning `apply_update_and_exit` thread.
- `crates/gwt/web/index.html`: `update_state` WebSocket handler, 8 s dismissable toast, `window.confirm` → `apply_update` send.

- [ ] Migration/backfill plan included — not applicable (no schema/data change)
- [x] CHANGELOG impact considered — `feat:` commit triggers minor version bump

## Context

- The Tauri-era self-update feature was removed in SPEC-1776 (TUI migration commit `18764cdb`).
- SPEC-2041 restores equivalent UX: the GUI shows a startup toast; CLI users use `gwt update`.
- `gwt __internal apply-update` / `gwt __internal run-installer` are post-exit subprocess helpers — they wait for the parent process to exit before swapping binaries, which avoids the Windows locked-file problem.

author: dimavedenyapin
body:
## Summary

- Opencode (and other fire-and-forget adapters) could transition a session to `idle` immediately after a follow-up message, before any response was produced. Users saw the task flip to *ready_for_review* with an empty transcript.
- Root cause: `startAdapterPolling` pre-set `hasSeenWork=true` whenever an `existingSession` was passed (for dedup-state preservation). The 15s IDLE grace period — introduced to handle the brief window between fire-and-forget `sendPrompt` and the backend actually registering the prompt — only fires when `hasSeenWork=false`, so it was silently skipped on every follow-up.
- Fix: always create polling entries with `hasSeenWork=false`. Dedup state (`seenMessageIds` / `seenPartIds` / `partContentLengths`) is still carried over from the existing session, so past messages aren't re-sent to the renderer.

### Observed symptoms
```
[AgentManager] Registered session ses_26f589a23ffeLhLU7kyQbfJnnz for polling (2 active)
[AgentManager] Detected IDLE status for ses_26f589a23ffeLhLU7kyQbfJnnz, calling transitionToIdle
[AgentManager] Unregistered session ses_26f589a23ffeLhLU7kyQbfJnnz from polling (1 remaining)
[AgentManager] Session ses_26f589a23ffeLhLU7kyQbfJnnz → idle
```

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/agent-manager.test.ts` — 50/50 pass (3 new regression tests)
- [x] `npx tsc --build --noEmit` — clean
- [ ] Manual: send a follow-up message to an opencode task and confirm the response renders instead of the session flipping to idle immediately
- [ ] Manual: brand-new opencode task still transitions to idle correctly after the real response completes

author: kidchenko
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The `tools/os_installers/apt.sh` script was downloading executable artifacts to predictable temporary paths like `/tmp/yq` or directly to the current working directory. This pattern is vulnerable to Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) and symlink attacks. If an attacker pre-creates a symlink at `/tmp/yq` pointing to a sensitive file, the script (running with `sudo`) could inadvertently overwrite it or allow local privilege escalation.
🎯 Impact: Local attackers could potentially escalate privileges or overwrite critical system files by exploiting the predictable download paths when the installation script is executed.
🔧 Fix: Wrapped the `go`, `yq`, and `lsd` installation blocks in subshells `(...)`. Within each subshell, a secure temporary directory is created using `TMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)`, and a local trap (`trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT`) ensures cleanup. The `wget` commands were updated to download specifically into this isolated directory.
✅ Verification: Ensure the scripts pass `shellcheck` (via `./build.sh lint`) and that running the modified installation blocks does not leave artifacts in `/tmp` or the current directory.

author: copilot
body:
Deployment was failing for the ADIF cleanse function with `Can't find the storage bucket region` because trigger bucket config could resolve to a non-existent fallback bucket. This PR updates trigger configuration to use only real configured bucket values and avoid invalid region lookups.

- **Trigger bucket resolution**
  - Removed synthetic fallback bucket derivation (`<project>.appspot.com` / local fallback behavior).
  - Added explicit bucket resolution from runtime config only:
    - `STORAGE_BUCKET`
    - `FIREBASE_CONFIG.storageBucket` (when present/parseable)

- **Trigger registration behavior**
  - Register `onObjectFinalized` with `{ bucket: configuredStorageBucket }` when a valid configured bucket exists.
  - Otherwise register with empty options (`{}`) so deployment succeeds without forcing bucket-region lookup at deploy discovery time.

- **Code structure/readability**
  - Extracted handler into `cleanseAdifHandler` and kept export wiring compact.
  - Preserved existing path-based gating (`parseOriginalPath`) so processing remains scoped to `*/original/*` objects.

```ts
const configuredStorageBucket = process.env.STORAGE_BUCKET ??
  JSON.parse(process.env.FIREBASE_CONFIG ?? "{}").storageBucket;

export const cleanseAdif = onObjectFinalized(
  configuredStorageBucket ? { bucket: configuredStorageBucket } : {},
  cleanseAdifHandler,
);
```

author: keiko713
body:
Use the `VolumeBytesUsed` CloudWatch metric (queried by `DBClusterIdentifier`) for Aurora instead of the previously inaccurate OS-level filesystem values or `AllocatedStorage`. This was wrongly reporting a few MB storage usage regardless of the actual cluster storage size.
With the `GetRdsClusterIntMetric` function (to obtain `VolumeBytesUsed` metric), use the 3 hours lookback window to retrieve the data reliably (see below for more detail).

In passing, update `AuroraMaxStorage` from 64TB to 128TB to reflect the current Aurora storage limit.

Several notes (likely worth noting this in the UI side):
* Aurora volume metrics like `VolumeBytesUsed` are [reported infrequently](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraMonitoring.Metrics.html) ("collected at intervals, not continuously"). In testing, a 10-minute window returned no data at all, and a 1-hour window still produced frequent gaps. A 3-hour window reliably returns data. When data is available, we pick the most recent datapoint.
  * This means that the data can be at max 3 hours old, also there might be still gap (will report 0B in that case)
* `VolumeBytesUsed` is only available as a cluster-level metric (dimension: `DBClusterIdentifier`), not per-instance.
  * This means all instances in the same cluster will report the same disk usage

This server is using this branch:
https://staging.pganalyze.com/servers/336fdc7yijartkopql6yerfisy/system/storage?t=24h

body:
### Motivation
- Improve detection of provider availability errors to better decide when to fallback to another provider. 
- Increase Gemini's reasoning budget and sampling control to improve analysis quality for deep mode. 
- Add Groq model candidate fallbacks and high-reasoning configuration to make deep analyses more resilient to model unavailability.

### Description
- Expand `isProviderUnavailableError` to recognize more failure phrases such as `service unavailable`, `model`, `not found`, `does not exist`, `decommissioned`, `unsupported`, and `rate limit`.
- For Gemini, set a larger thinking budget via `thinkingConfig: { thinkingBudget: 24576 }` and add `topP: 0.5` to the generation config to tune sampling.
- For Groq, replace the single-model selection with `modelCandidates` arrays for `deep` and `quick` modes and iterate through them, adding `reasoning_effort: "high"`, `top_p: 0.5`, and retry logic that uses `isProviderUnavailableError` to decide whether to try the next model; rethrow the final error if all candidates fail.
- Change the public fallback logic in `analyzeText` to use `isProviderUnavailableError` (provider-agnostic) when deciding whether to attempt the fallback provider.

### Testing
- Ran TypeScript build with `npm run build` (`tsc`) and it succeeded.
- Ran unit tests with `npm test` and they passed.
- Ran a smoke integration of `analyzeText` exercising fallback behavior and it completed without errors.

author: ahmadmsaleem
body:
### Problem
`wait` / `halt` only work as effects today, they block the entire trigger until the delay elapses. There is no way in Skript to schedule a block of code to run later while the rest of the trigger continues immediately.

### Solution
Make Delay an EffectSection. EffectSectionEffect delegated setNext/getNext but not getActualNext or executionIntent, so Section.loadCode's intent walk stopped at the wrapper and missed trailing stop intents — letting inner delays leak past the section. Override both to delegate.

Effect form: unchanged.

Section form: body parses as a separate trigger under outer events with hasDelayBefore=TRUE. walk() snapshots locals, schedules the task, swaps locals in the callback so mutations stay isolated. Outer isn't delayed.



### Testing Completed
Manual in game testing on a Paper server covering:
```applescript

#Skript wait effect tests
#These tests cover various scenarios of the wait effect, including nested waits, variable scope, and interaction with loops and functions. 
#The expected outputs are provided as comments for verification.



command /test1:
    trigger:
        broadcast "A"
        wait 1 second:
            broadcast "B"
            wait 2 seconds:
                broadcast "C"
            broadcast "D"
            wait 1 second
            broadcast "E"
        broadcast "F"
# expect: A, F, (1s) B, D, (2s) E, (3s) C


command /test2:
    trigger:
        set {_shared} to "outer"
        loop 3 times:
            set {_i} to loop-number
            wait 1 second:
                set {_shared} to "body-%{_i}%"
                broadcast "iter %{_i}% shared=%{_shared}% %unix timestamp of now%"
        wait 2 seconds
        broadcast "done shared=%{_shared}% %unix timestamp of now%"
# expect: (1s) 3 messages "iter 1..3" each with correct number and shared=body-N, (3s after start) done shared=outer


command /test3:
    trigger:
        broadcast "1"
        wait 2 seconds
        broadcast "2"
# expect: 1, (2s) 2 — effect form unchanged


command /test4:
    trigger:
        wait 1 second:
            broadcast "Inside wait: A"
            stop
            broadcast "Inside wait: B" # This shouldn't run
        broadcast "Outside wait"
# expect: Outside wait, (1s) Inside wait: A


command /test5:
    trigger:
        wait 1 second:
            set {_count} to 0
            while {_count} < 3:
                broadcast "Background tick: %{_count}%"
                add 1 to {_count}
                wait 1 second # The normal wait effect inside the section
        broadcast "Trigger finished, background task starting..."
# expect: (1s) Background tick: 0, (2s) Background tick: 1, (3s) Background tick: 2, (3s) Trigger finished, background task starting...


command /test6:
    trigger:
        add "A", "B" and "C" to {_list::*}
        wait 1 second:
            broadcast "Inside wait, list is: %{_list::*}%"
        delete {_list::*}
        broadcast "Deleted list outside."
# expect: Deleted list outside., (1s) Inside wait, list is: A, B and C. 
# BUG POTENTIAL: If local list variables aren't deep-copied properly into the section's local scope, it might print <none>.



command /test7:
    trigger:
        testWaitReturn()
        broadcast "Function finished."

function testWaitReturn():
    wait 1 second:
        broadcast "Function wait running."
# expect: Function finished., (1s) Function wait running. (And no console errors).
```

[15:31:06 INFO]: A
[15:31:06 INFO]: F
[15:31:07 INFO]: B
[15:31:07 INFO]: D

> test2

[15:31:10 INFO]: iter 3 shared=body-3 1778938270.4

No skript test files added in this PR `wait` / `halt` do not currently have test scripts under `src/test/skript/tests/` and adding the first ones for this feature felt out of scope. Happy to add them in a follow up

author: chinmay-kulkarni-amd
body:
## Purpose
Update the AMD Zen CPU platform (`ZenCpuPlatform`) to correctly declare supported dtypes and switch the zentorch dependency to the weekly release channel.
This PR fixes the two minor issues introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35089
1. **Declare `supported_dtypes` for Zen CPU**: AMD Zen CPUs do not support float16 compute natively. The base `CpuPlatform` includes `torch.float16` in its `supported_dtypes`, which causes vLLM to accept float16 models on Zen CPUs. This leads to dtype mismatches and the execution errors out. This PR overrides `supported_dtypes` in `ZenCpuPlatform` to return only `[torch.bfloat16, torch.float32]`, matching the actual hardware capabilities.
2. **Switch `vllm[zen]` to `zentorch-weekly`**: The `zentorch` PyPI release cadence is weekly. Using `zentorch-weekly` ensures `pip install vllm[zen]` always pulls the known-good version of weekly build instead of release builds.
## Test Plan
- Verify that models with native float16 dtype (e.g., `bloom-560m`, `opt-125m`) are automatically resolved to bfloat16 on Zen CPU with a warning, instead of silently running in an unsupported dtype.
- Run the existing CPU generation tests on an AMD Zen machine:
  ```bash
  pytest -v -s tests/models/language/generation -m cpu_model
- Verify pip install vllm[zen] resolves to the latest zentorch-weekly package.
- Verify that the test cases added specifically for Zen CPU and zentorch can run and pass.
  ```bash
  pytest tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py -v
  pytest tests/model_executor/test_cpu_unquantized_gemm_dispatch.py -v
 
## Test Result
- Models with torch_dtype=float16 in their HF config are correctly downcast to bfloat16 with a log warning: Your device 'cpu' doesn't support torch.float16. Falling back to torch.bfloat16 for compatibility.
- Models with torch_dtype=bfloat16 or torch_dtype=float32 are unaffected.
- pip install "vllm[zen]" successfully installs zentorch-weekly.
- Test cases added specifically for Zen CPU and zentorch run and pass successfully.
```bash
