body:
## Motivation
- langchain-community was a hard runtime dependency of langchain-cohere, but it's only used by create_sql_agent in langchain_cohere/sql_agent/agent.py. 
- Every user who installed langchain-cohere just to use ChatCohere, CohereEmbeddings, or CohereRerank was forced to pull in the entire langchain-community package and its transitive dependencies.

## Changes
- pyproject.toml: Removed langchain-community from [tool.poetry.dependencies]. It remains in the test and typing dependency groups.
- sql_agent/agent.py: Moved the langchain-community imports (SQLDatabaseToolkit, InfoSQLDatabaseTool, ListSQLDatabaseTool) from the module top-level into the create_sql_agent function body behind a try/except ImportError that raises a clear install instruction. Type-checking imports are preserved under TYPE_CHECKING for static analysis.
- __init__.py: Replaced the eager import of create_sql_agent with a __getattr__-based lazy import, so importing the package no longer triggers the sql_agent module (and therefore no longer requires langchain-community at import time).

## Validation
- Full test suite passes (poetry run pytest -v): 158 passed, 2 skipped, 5 xfailed.
- from langchain_cohere import ChatCohere, CohereEmbeddings, CohereRerank no longer triggers any langchain-community imports.
- from langchain_cohere import create_sql_agent still works when langchain-community is installed, and raises a clear ImportError with install instructions when it isn't.
- No behavior changes for existing users who have langchain-community installed.

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52L53-R58) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43d27a085d7ede064c4964b1e58aa579b041a20c431b056b47ef2d7bddbcaf3eR1-R56) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2a0bd95cec288dfd966542e6dba2a9da2041ab8fc8b1f8e23e1171b3622c2f82R1-R30) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ccb103095e525d10fbb111a4a76ad3e81b7c655c9ccb9530f4a084c2a939e749R1-R13) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-fbffc5ad09bc0c9223367fe20c062860810fb6efab88643d0291c0a1a321c16cR1-R15)

**Executor and function signature refactoring:**

* Refactored executor and related functions to consistently use `t_shelly *` (pointer) instead of `t_shelly` (by value), ensuring correct state management and memory safety across the codebase. This includes changes to `executor`, `exec_simple_command`, `find_path`, `find_command`, and pipe execution functions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a93cb515f0980f725dbf5f3acac87671e9c06b51de5a416a79327006956ef72dL113-R123) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d6d6d05cd7f49099c9b442ca19909a126e7de8e2266db9237f1641603e6e35a1L9-R38) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d6d6d05cd7f49099c9b442ca19909a126e7de8e2266db9237f1641603e6e35a1R47-R61) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d6d6d05cd7f49099c9b442ca19909a126e7de8e2266db9237f1641603e6e35a1L65-R109) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-82ef828532e422439afa787add5b7b1b951b3b50d3dde643e6a30d641b64f80cL9-R24) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-82ef828532e422439afa787add5b7b1b951b3b50d3dde643e6a30d641b64f80cL41-R43) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-82ef828532e422439afa787add5b7b1b951b3b50d3dde643e6a30d641b64f80cL57-R53)

* Added a `sanitize` target to the Makefile, enabling compilation with AddressSanitizer (`-fsanitize=address`) for easier detection of memory leaks during development.

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52L53-R58) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52R95-R101)

author: mrmemo87-cell
body:
### Motivation
- Superadmins could enter admin mode in the app via `rpc_is_superadmin` but were blocked by admin RPCs (e.g. `rpc_admin_grant`) because `is_current_user_admin()` only checked `users.is_admin` / `users.role = 'admin'`. 
- This mismatch caused superadmins to receive `forbidden` when attempting grants (coins/XP) even though the UI allowed admin actions.

### Description
- Updated the helper `is_current_user_admin()` to also allow `is_superadmin(auth.uid())` so superadmins are treated as admins for server-side RPC authorization. 
- Applied the same change in both `supabase-functions/competition_phase1.sql` and `DEPLOY_COMPETITION_PHASE1.sql` to keep source and deployment scripts consistent. 
- This change enables existing admin RPCs (including `rpc_admin_grant`) to accept superadmins without altering other role checks.

### Testing
- Verified the updated predicate appears in both files using code search with `rg -n "is_current_user_admin|is_superadmin(auth.uid())"`, and the search confirmed the new `or is_superadmin(auth.uid())` clause in both SQL files (success). 
- Inspected the modified SQL snippets to confirm `rpc_admin_grant` still enforces `is_current_user_admin()` before performing updates (success). 
- No unit tests were added or run as part of this change; only static verification and file inspection were performed (informational).

body:
## Summary
Tracking 로그에서 branch / join 흐름을 존 접두사 기반으로 별도 파일로 분기 기록함. 기존 통합 `process.log` 는 그대로 유지되어 기존 분석/모니터링 경로 호환이 보장됨.

## 동작

| zone 접두사 | 기록 파일 |
| --- | --- |
| `branch_*` | `branch.log` + `process.log` |
| `join_*` | `join.log` + `process.log` |
| 그 외 | `process.log` |

## 설정 (`config/base.yaml`)

```yaml
log_dir:
  root: "logs"
  process: "process"
  monitor: "monitor"
  branch: "branch"   # null 이면 해당 split 비활성
  join: "join"       # null 이면 해당 split 비활성
```

프로파일에서 `branch: ~` / `join: ~` 로 override 하여 분기 로그를 끌 수 있음.

## 플랫폼 독립성
표준 `logging` / `os` / `datetime` 만 사용. OS 조건 분기 없음. 개발 환경과 운영 서버 동일 동작.

## Fallback 안전장치 (메시지 유실 방지)

| 실패 경로 | 대응 |
| --- | --- |
| 알 수 없는 `log_type` 이 Logger API 에 전달 | `process` 로 복구 + `stderr` 경고 |
| branch/join 폴더 생성 실패 (권한/디스크 등) | 해당 split 만 비활성화, 통합 `process.log` 는 정상 동작 |
| config 값이 비문자열 등 잘못된 타입 | 해당 split 무시 + 경고 |
| branch/join 폴더명이 null/빈 문자열 | 해당 split 비활성 (경고 없이) |

모든 실패 경로에서 **통합 로그 (process.log) 는 영향 받지 않음** — 이벤트 유실 방지.

## 하위 호환성
- `ProcessLogger.log_*` API 에 `log_type` 키워드 인자 기본값 추가
- 기존 호출부 (`self.log_info(msg)`) 수정 없이 이전과 동일 동작
- `process.log` 는 모든 트래킹 이벤트를 여전히 통합 기록

## 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| 유닛 테스트 (신규 28 케이스) | **28/28 PASS** |
| 로컬 E2E (실제 로거/이벤트 emit → 파일 내용 검증) | **PASS** (branch/join/process 정확 분리) |
| 플랫폼 의존 코드 스캔 | 없음 |
| 하드코딩 경로 스캔 | 없음 |


## 실제 비디오 파이프라인 검증

합성 이벤트가 아닌 `branch_short.mp4` (640x360, 25fps, 30초, 750 프레임) 을
CPU YOLO + 원본 Tracker + SSBR_branch+join 프로파일로 돌린 실제 결과.

### 파일별 기록량

| 파일 | 크기 | EventService 이벤트 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logs/branch/<ts>.log` | 342 B | **2** (branch_out_b 탈출 2회) |
| `logs/join/<ts>.log` | 2.9 KB | **18** (join_in_a create / final_baler 등) |
| `logs/process/<ts>.log` | 14.6 KB | **27** (통합 로그 — branch/join/기타 모두) |

### 숫자 일관성

- branch 2 + join 18 = **20개** 가 zone prefix 매칭으로 분기 로그에 기록
- process 27 - 20 = **7개** 는 zone=None 또는 기타 zone 으로 process.log 에만
- 트랙 lifecycle (create / removed / exited / final_baler) 모두 완결

### 샘플 로그 발췌

**branch.log (2건 전체):**
```
[EventService] Track Exited: '1/.../join_in_a/.../branch_out_b' → 'branch_out_b'
[EventService] Track Exited: '7/.../join_in_a/.../branch_out_b' → 'branch_out_b'
```

**join.log (앞 4건):**
```
[EventService] Track Exited: '0/.../None/.../join_out' → 'join_out'
[EventService] Track Created: '1/.../join_in_a/...'
[EventService] Track Created: '2/.../join_in_a/...'
[EventService] Track Final Baler: '2/.../join_in_a/...' in 'join_in_a'
```

**process.log (전체 27건 축약, branch/join/기타 포함):**
```
Track Created (9) + Track Exited (3) + Track Removed (5) + Track Final Baler (10)
```

### 기존 분석 도구 호환 확인

`process.log` 에 모든 이벤트가 통합 기록되므로, 기존 grep/파싱 스크립트는
**수정 없이 그대로** 동작. 분기 분석이 필요할 때만 `branch/` 또는 `join/`
폴더를 추가로 참조하면 됨.

## 변경 파일

| 파일 | 내용 |
| --- | --- |
| `src/rubber_tracker/utils/logger.py` | `LogTypeFilter` 확장, `_normalize_log_type`, `_prepare_split_log_file`, branch/join 핸들러 조건부 생성, `ProcessLogger.log_*` 에 `log_type` kwarg 추가 |
| `src/rubber_tracker/track/services/core/event_service.py` | `_zone_to_log_type` 헬퍼 추가, `build_event` 에서 zone 기반 log_type 결정 |
| `config/base.yaml` | `log_dir` 에 `branch`, `join` 필드 추가 |
| `tests/test_log_split.py` | 신규 28 케이스 (라우팅 + fallback 엣지) |
| `tests/conftest.py` | 개발 환경 stub (Hailo/GStreamer 없는 환경에서 pytest 실행 가능) |
| `.gitignore` | `tests/*` 하위 기본 제외 + 허용 파일 예외 |

## Test plan
- [x] 유닛 테스트 28/28 PASS
- [x] 로컬 E2E (파일 기반 라우팅 정확성)
- [x] fallback 엣지 케이스 6종 (null/빈/비문자열/OSError/unknown log_type/빈 집합)
- [x] 플랫폼 독립 확인
- [ ] 운영 환경 스모크 테스트

## 참고
`tests/conftest.py` 는 동일 PR 시리즈의 `feat(event_image_saver)` / `feat(log_cleaner)` PR 과 내용이 동일함. 어느 쪽이 먼저 머지되어도 동일 파일로 충돌 없이 통합 가능함.

💡 What: Replaces `os.path.commonpath` with a much faster `str.startswith()` comparison in `helpers.files.is_in_dir()`.
🎯 Why: `os.path.commonpath` is a significant performance bottleneck due to underlying path splitting algorithms and internal list allocations.
📊 Impact: ~3.7x faster path containment checks (a critical helper used widely across the filesystem logic).
🔬 Measurement: Verified with a `timeit` script comparing the two paths traversing 100,000 times, dropping from ~0.71s to ~0.19s. Ensures directory containment by verifying strict match or suffixing with trailing path separator.

author: widthdom
body:
## Summary
- Closes meta-issue #384 by adding a "Design Decision — C# Extraction Ceiling (Issue #384)" section to `SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md` in both English and Japanese.
- Decision: **Hybrid, with Option B as the primary direction** — extend the already-hand-written `StructuralLineMasker` into a richer per-line scanner that additionally exposes enclosing class/method stack, brace/paren/angle-bracket depth, logical declaration start line, and carry-over `in_string` / `in_comment` flags, so the C# extraction layer (`SymbolExtractor` + `ReferenceExtractor`) regex consumers can query scope state instead of re-parsing it ad-hoc.
- Option A (externalizing per-language regex tables into data files) is **deferred, not rejected** — current pain is driven by cross-construct regex interactions on C# / Java, not language breadth, and data-table externalization does not remove those interactions.
- **No dependency-rule exception**: the extension stays hand-written, following the precedent set by `StructuralLineMasker` and the JS/TS lexer. No Roslyn, no tree-sitter, no new production NuGet package.
- Explicit exit criteria list which open issues should close or become materially simpler once the scanner exposes scope + declaration-start state:
  - Multi-line declarations: #361, #382
  - String/comment bleed beyond the current masker: #264, #274, #288, #291, #301, #363, #372
  - Nested initializer / bracket tracking: #257, #286, #293, #330
  - Scope attribution: #233, #242, #252, #316
- Non-goals: a full C# parser; simultaneous language rewrite. C# lands first (dogfooding priority), Java follows only where syntax overlap makes the port trivial.
- Workflow implication: the next landing C# / Java reference-extractor fix from the exit-criteria list should be treated as the first real consumer of the extended scanner so the API is shaped by a concrete fix rather than designed in isolation.
- CHANGELOG entries (English and Japanese) added under `[Unreleased]` → Added.

## Scope
Documentation only. No code, tests, or CLI/MCP behavior changes. Per #384's own acceptance criteria, the closing condition is a recorded design decision — this PR satisfies that by committing the decision, exit criteria, and dependency-rule note to `SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet build` passes with 0 warnings / 0 errors.
- [x] Local index refresh (`index . --commits HEAD --json`) succeeds after the commit.
- [x] No U+FFFD replacement characters introduced in edited files.
- [x] English and Japanese sections of `SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` stay in sync.
- [x] Adversarial review via `codex exec --ephemeral` (round 2) reports no blocking/actionable findings.

Closes #384

body:
This pull request introduces several significant improvements to CI governance, workflow validation, and nomenclature enforcement, while also cleaning up deprecated workflows and updating documentation for modality support. The main themes are: (1) new CI governance and policy enforcement, (2) workflow and nomenclature quality checks, (3) governance event schema validation, (4) removal of deprecated CI workflows, and (5) documentation and taxonomy updates for modalities.

**CI Governance and Policy Enforcement:**

* Adds a new `ci-policy` composite GitHub Action and workflow (`.github/actions/ci-policy/action.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci-policy.yml`) to validate CI workflow policy per ADR-035, including advisory rollout and integration into PR review. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-43fc29966e2f4d65fa5e64da10919c9b068c4549c74bbd53a970d8b4ec99cf39R1-R30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-acf932ff0c0e41c1beda5df68fcc404e19c7d94a2206809c29ad03ab5989eea7R1-R40)
* Introduces a dedicated PR template for CI workflow changes, including a governance checklist and audit metadata requirements. (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ci_workflow_template.md`)
* Updates `CODEOWNERS` to assign CI governance ownership to the appropriate teams. (`.github/CODEOWNERS`)

**Workflow and Nomenclature Quality Checks:**

* Adds a new STD-001 nomenclature enforcement step and a generated report local-path guard to both PR and main CI workflows, ensuring report hygiene and naming consistency. (`.github/workflows/ci-pr.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci-main.yml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d7f7c1fd6d4e4da806b57e0d5a1bee46c0f8654468beedd7d571b91761474ff9R56-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a1a3cb9bdeb5541d148091d973cf266aa3b317e6415a86630e816cbe27cf8b9cR43-R47) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a1a3cb9bdeb5541d148091d973cf266aa3b317e6415a86630e816cbe27cf8b9cR121-R125)
* Ensures that relevant quality and nomenclature reports are uploaded as CI artifacts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d7f7c1fd6d4e4da806b57e0d5a1bee46c0f8654468beedd7d571b91761474ff9R75-R76) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a1a3cb9bdeb5541d148091d973cf266aa3b317e6415a86630e816cbe27cf8b9cR136)

**Governance Event Schema Validation:**

* Adds a conditional workflow to detect changes relevant to governance event schemas and runs schema validation and tests only when necessary, improving CI efficiency and compliance with ADR-028. (`.github/workflows/ci-pr.yml`)

**CI Workflow Cleanup:**

* Removes deprecated `coverage.yml` and `dependency-audit.yml` workflows as part of CI modernization. (`.github/workflows/coverage.yml`, `.github/workflows/dependency-audit.yml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a2115d277b5ca5a2f09a999e53440839cf332b94da177f3d1766334555b0f7c6L1-L22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-781c7519f37eabca5a2dea4e7a2fb39ad94e7b84f0cc5559b17dc44dba7c82e6L1-L54)

**Modality and Documentation Updates:**

* Updates modality extension documentation to remove support for `"timeseries"`, clarifying canonical and alias modality names across multiple skill docs. (`.claude/skills/ce-modality-extension/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/ce-plugin-audit/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/ce-plugin-scaffold/SKILL.md`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-17f332c9d87e334ba7e439b1aaace019d96162255ad1ba0117673d17d249bf42L4-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-17f332c9d87e334ba7e439b1aaace019d96162255ad1ba0117673d17d249bf42L33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9ea34ef3d27a673a50c3c30ad1a1dbda56e7e23b849c04b50e788385f867ff51L144-R148) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b26496e1d359c3ca65c3dac1f77d9ecc7636af8fdb7926f06c3d50ea0a37a71fL5-R5)
* Corrects deprecation table entries for `old_param` in migration docs. (`.claude/skills/ce-deprecation/SKILL.md`)

**Other Notable Changes:**

* Refactors nightly CI workflows for improved clarity and separation between example runs and notebook execution, with advisory and artifact upload steps. (`.github/workflows/ci-nightly.yml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-615cb3ee1eed561019f2656233213805547944435e6d6f6907503751d4e5e7baL47-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-615cb3ee1eed561019f2656233213805547944435e6d6f6907503751d4e5e7baL61-R83) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-615cb3ee1eed561019f2656233213805547944435e6d6f6907503751d4e5e7baL92-R116)

## Summary
- make Fluent `SentMessage` parsing resilient when ABI decoding returns incomplete values
- if parsed payload has empty `message_hash` or `nonce`, fall back to raw-bytes decoding
- add warning log for dropped `SentMessage` records with tx hash and data size, to debug live chains quickly

## Why
Some live bridge logs can be parsed into incomplete structs even though the topic is correct. Those items were silently dropped later because `message_hash` became nil, which looked like the indexer was "ignoring" events.

## Expected effect
- previously skipped `SentMessage` events should now be imported
- operators get explicit warning logs when an event is still malformed

## Post-review adjustments (2026-04-18, commits `feb8bf9`–`38ca605`)

Post-review polish pass after Max's first-round feedback.

### What changed

**Ballot reframed as async-decision instrument.** The trigger is async decision-making (review over chat, on a PR, on a train, remote handoff), not reviewer count. Single-decider async is now a first-class use case; multi-reviewer panels still get per-reviewer files. Updated SKILL.md description, README intro, conventions rationale, template (peer ballot line made optional), marketplace entry, root README skills table, and the `dossier` → `ballot` cross-reference.

**Six overfit audit hooks removed; two kept.** `dossier-citation-audit`, `dossier-forbidden-words`, `dossier-section-order`, `dossier-dated-claim-scan`, `ballot-anti-option`, and `ballot-cover-archaeology` each encoded patterns specific to the a11y-extension session (`[Xn]` citation style, OSS-mode wordlist, H2-level glossary heading, specific archaeology phrases). Dossiers in other styles use different conventions; the grep gates either missed real failures or fired spurious ones. Kept `ballot-filename.sh` and `dossier-framing-declared.sh` — mechanical checks that generalize. Dispatcher simplified (shims JSON-stdin to argv; no more routing logic — each kept script self-gates).

**Two reviewer-checklists replace the grep gates.** `skills/dossier/references/review-checklist.md` (8 items, ~180 lines): framing coherence, citation integrity, dated-claim freshness, section ordering, source bias flagging, hyperlink density, selectivity, Key Facts box accuracy. `skills/ballot/references/review-checklist.md` (8 items, ~150 lines): filename pattern, cover-block cleanliness, anti-options, time-horizon-per-DEC, recommended-not-pre-ticked, tier discipline, async-readability, reconciliation location. Each item is structured as what-to-check / why it matters / what good looks like / red flags so a reviewer can apply without invention.

**Reference files cleaned up.** `framing-modes.yaml` deleted (orphaned once `forbidden-words.sh` was removed; no remaining consumer). `audit-checks.md` deleted (80% documented deleted scripts). `framing-modes.md` kept as mode-selection guide with inline vocabulary examples replacing the YAML pointer.

### What to re-review (~8 min)

1. **`skills/ballot/SKILL.md`** (3 min) — the reframe. `When to Use`, `When NOT to Use`, and the `Reviewing a ballot` section are the most changed.
2. **`skills/dossier/references/review-checklist.md`** + **`skills/ballot/references/review-checklist.md`** (4 min) — the new grep-gate replacement. Skim the 8 items in each; each should be a concern a reviewer would genuinely raise.
3. **`.claude-plugin/hooks/dossier-hook-dispatcher.sh`** (1 min) — simplified to an argv/stdin shim.

### Changeset

`.changeset/20260418-130906-polish-pass.md` — `minor` bump for both `ballot` and `dossier` (user-visible framing change; new review mechanism; no breaking changes).

### Sessionlog

`docs/sessionlogs/2026-04-18-pitch-b-impl.md` appended with a `## Post-review Polish` section documenting the 9 decisions (P1–P9), file change list, and hook test matrix.


### Follow-up: clickable citations (commits `517157c`–`9b2d1df`)

One more concrete change in the same pass. The `[Xn]` citation convention is upgraded to Markdown reference-link syntax: body carries `claim [S1][ref-S1]`, §Sources carries both the verbal entry and a `[ref-S1]: https://...` definition at the bottom. Renders as a clickable `S1` link in GitHub/Obsidian/Bitbucket/Confluence; raw markdown keeps the `[S1]` bracket token for direct file readers.

Two trade-offs documented in the sessionlog (decisions C1–C4):

- **Reference-link over footnote `[^S1]`.** Footnote rendering is uneven across target renderers (many mobile readers, Confluence internal renderers, and terminal previewers skip them). Reference-links parse identically everywhere. Footnote form documented as an alternative for authors whose target renderer supports it.

author: nevradonatwork
body:
## Summary
Modified the game results sorting logic to prioritize games where it's the user's turn, improving the user experience by surfacing active games first.

## Key Changes
- Added `.sort()` to the game results array that orders games by `isMyTurn` status
- Games where it's the user's turn (`isMyTurn: true`) are sorted to the beginning
- Games where it's not the user's turn are sorted to the end

## Implementation Details
The sort comparator `(a, b) => (b.isMyTurn ? 1 : 0) - (a.isMyTurn ? 1 : 0)` works by:
- Converting boolean `isMyTurn` values to numeric values (1 for true, 0 for false)
- Comparing `b` before `a` to achieve descending order (user's turn games first)
- This ensures games requiring user action are displayed prominently in the results list

## Summary
Bumps OAS pin from v0.159.0 to v0.160.0 (jeong-sik/oas#998 e5ec2d1a) to pick up:

author: cocorof
body:
## Summary

v0.8.8 shipped the visual work (Required badge, `.inactive` mute style, header source label) but two upstream data-path bugs silently made the fixes unreachable — so after merging v0.8.8 the UI still showed every stage green and a toggleable Active checkbox on required stages. This PR fixes the data path so v0.8.8's UI actually renders.

### What was actually broken

- **Required badge unreachable.** The library emits `required: True` for s01_input / s06_api / s09_parse / s16_yield (≥0.13.3), but `StageIntrospectionResponse` didn't list the field. FastAPI dropped it on the way out (Pydantic v2 `extra='ignore'`). `StageCard.isRequired` was therefore always false.
- **Bypassed stages rendered green.** `executionStore` merged `stage.bypass` into `completedStages`. `PipelineView`'s class priority `active > error > completed > inactive` then won on `.completed` before ever reaching `.inactive`, so every bypassed stage — including manifest-inactive ones — painted green.

### Fixes

1. **`backend/app/schemas/catalog.py`** — add `required: bool = False` to `StageIntrospectionResponse`. The library's flag now reaches every catalog endpoint (bootstrap, per-artifact, introspection cache). Additive, safe default for older backends.
2. **`frontend/src/stores/executionStore.ts`** — introduce `bypassedStages: Set<string>`. `stage.bypass` no longer pollutes `completedStages`. `reset()` clears both.
3. **`frontend/src/components/pipeline/PipelineView.tsx`** — subscribe `bypassedStages` and change the priority to `active > error > completed > (bypassed || inactive)`. Both "didn't run" conditions share the existing `.inactive` style.
4. **`backend/app/routers/session.py`** — `GET /api/sessions/{id}` now describes the session's live pipeline via `session.pipeline.describe()` instead of rebuilding from the preset name. Closes a latent `ValueError: Unknown preset` for env-backed sessions registered under the synthetic `"env:<id>"` label.
5. **`backend/tests/conftest.py`** — fake session now exposes `pipeline.describe()` returning real `StageDescription` dataclass instances so the updated GET handler works under the existing test harness.

### Env → runtime fidelity audit (Stage C in the plan)

A short static audit confirmed that `Pipeline.from_manifest` already respects `entry.active` (inactive stages are never registered, not in `_stages`, reported `is_active=False` by `describe()`), and `PipelineMutator.restore` correctly propagates per-stage `config` into `stage.get_config()`. The "inactive stages look active" observation was the same bypass-conflation bug above, not a manifest/runtime leak. No runtime-behaviour change needed there.

## Test plan

- [x] Backend `pytest` — 51/51 pass
- [x] Frontend `tsc -b --noEmit` — clean
- [x] Library -> Pydantic round-trip: `required=True` preserved for orders 1/6/9/16
- [x] `Pipeline.from_manifest(manifest_with_stage_10_inactive)` — stage 10 absent from `_stages`, reported `is_active=False`
- [x] `stage.config` round-trip — manifest `{'stateless': True}` reaches `ContextStage.get_config()`
- [ ] Manual: Builder renders Required badge on stages 1/6/9/16 (no Active checkbox)
- [ ] Manual: run `agent` preset — bypassed stages stay muted, only active stages turn green
- [ ] Manual: run an env with stage 10 disabled — stage 10 stays muted, not green

author: zkoesters
body:
Tested locally with `renovate --dry-run=full`. Two issues found and fixed.

## 1. Spurious `extractVersion` capture in `depName`

The `(?<depName>.*?)` capture in `matchStrings` was non-greedy but the trailing `\\s+extractVersion=(?<extractVersion>.*?)` pattern wasn't matching (Renovate doesn't support `extractVersion` as a named capture group). This caused the entire remainder of the comment line — `GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom extractVersion=^GE-Proton(?<version>.+)$` — to be slurped into `depName`, making the GitHub API lookup fail with `no-result`.

Fix: remove `extractVersion=...` from the comment and the `matchStrings` regex entirely.

## 2. Wrong versioning scheme (`semver-coerced` → `loose`)

After stripping the `GE-Proton` prefix, versions are `10-34`, `10-15` etc. — `MAJOR-MINOR` with a hyphen. `semver-coerced` (the default) can't parse these, so Renovate found no updates. Adding `"versioningTemplate": "loose"` handles arbitrary version strings and correctly orders `10-34` > `10-15`.

Both confirmed via dry run: dep is detected as `depName: "GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom"`, `versioning: "loose"`, `currentValue: "10-15"`, and the `10-34` release is available as an update.

author: lucabol
body:
Updates `deps/laststanding` from `cb8b087` → `5659406` for the TLS handshake freeze fix, audits Oscan's TLS wrappers against the new semantics, and adds an HTTPS example + integration test that fetches `https://www.lucabol.com/` and `https://text.npr.org/`.

## What's in 5659406

Two bugs fixed in `l_tls.h`:

1. **Handshake freeze on fragmented records.** `l_tls_do_handshake` had an inverted `if (ss != SEC_E_INCOMPLETE_MESSAGE)` guard that skipped `recv()` exactly when SChannel needed more bytes to finish a partial TLS record. Servers with larger cert chains (e.g. `text.npr.org`) could CPU-spin forever. Now always reads more data per iteration with a buffer-full bail.
2. **Clean close_notify handling.** `SEC_I_CONTEXT_EXPIRED` from `DecryptMessage` is now treated as graceful EOF — any in-band `SECBUFFER_DATA` is still delivered, then `l_tls_recv` returns `0`.

## Oscan wrapper audit

`runtime/osc_runtime.c:4337-4347` already uses `if (n <= 0)` for `osc_tls_recv`, so the new "returns 0 on clean close" semantics are handled correctly without wrapper changes. `osc_tls_recv_byte` inherits correct behavior via `n == 1` check in `l_tls_recv_byte`. No runtime or semantic-layer changes needed.

## Added

- `examples/https_get.osc` — HTTPS GET CLI (`https_get <host> [path]`).
- `tests/positive/tls_fetch.osc` — deterministic test fetching both hosts, validating HTTP/1.x 200 + non-empty body, printing `lucabol: ok\nnpr: ok`.
- `tests/expected/tls_fetch.expected` and `tests/expected_libc/tls_fetch.expected` (libc mode has no TLS backend → reports `connect_failed`).

## test.ps1

- Extended the freestanding DLL allowlist so `tls_*` tests may depend on `SECUR32.dll` / `CRYPT32.dll` (in addition to `KERNEL32` / `WS2_32`).
- WSL freestanding phase links `packaging/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/libbearssl.a` for `tls_*` tests.

author: realmeylisdev
body:
Closes #3093.

## Why

The old loader read `assets/seed_data/seed_events.sql` and ran it through `String.split(';')` before calling `db.customStatement` on each chunk. The splitter had no notion of SQL string literals, so a single seed row whose tags JSON contained `"ig; phaxn"` (an Instagram handle in a Vine author name) tore the INSERT apart at the embedded `;`. The remaining fragment had an unterminated `'...'` and SQLite rejected it with `unrecognized token: "'[[..."`. Because every insert ran inside one `db.transaction`, the failure rolled back **all** seed data — the local DB stayed empty, and the same error logged on every cold start until the app fetched from the relay.

The generator was already escaping `'` → `''` correctly, so single quotes were never the real issue. The title's fix — parameterize — is still the right long-term move because it removes the entire class of splitter / escape bugs.

## What changed

- **New asset**: `mobile/assets/seed_data/seed_events.json` (events + profile rows + metric rows). ~767KB vs ~819KB SQL.
- **Loader** (`SeedDataPreloadService`): loads JSON, binds every column through `db.customInsert(..., variables: [Variable.with...])`, keeps the one-shot transaction and the no-op-when-non-empty guard. `DateTime` columns use `Variable.withDateTime`, so Drift's default unix-epoch encoding is in play end-to-end (the old path wrote ISO strings into int-typed columns, which would have broken reads even if the split had worked).
- **Generator** (`scripts/generate_seed_data.dart`): emits JSON for future relay-driven regenerations.
- **Tests**: mock asset is JSON; added round-trip coverage for semicolons in tags, single quotes in content, brackets/backslashes, malformed JSON.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/services/seed_data_preload_service_test.dart` — 8/8 pass
- [x] `flutter test test/services/` — 1759/1759 pass
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test scripts` — clean
- [x] Pre-commit hook (format + analyze) ran green on commit
- [ ] Manual smoke on a fresh install — confirm seed count matches `meta.events` and no error logs

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- `docs/plans/2025-01-11-seed-data-preload*.md` still reference the SQL asset; left as historical design notes per the "older docs can drift" convention.
- Abandoned branch `origin/fix/seed-data-sql-escaping` (empty-tree commit `f87db4288`, @mbradley) can be deleted.

body:
## Summary

- Replace the single global phase with independent **carousel-level phase** (`settled | scrolling | snapping | locked`) and **per-item phase** (`settled | tracking | inertia | snapping`)
- Remove `focusedItemId` — the active item is identified by scanning for the item in `tracking` state
- Add `locked` carousel phase: entered from `settled` when a gesture targets an item; exits on `release` back to `settled`; motions without `itemId` are ignored while locked
- Items animate independently of the carousel phase (parallel operation): an item can coast in `inertia` while the carousel scrolls or snaps
- Add item-level `snapping` for under-zoom recovery: when scale < 1 on release, the item springs back to `{ x: 0, y: 0, scale: 1 }`

Design decisions documented in #7.

- [ ] Releasing a pinched item while under-zoomed triggers `snapping` → springs back to scale=1

body:
Adds the membership-read companion to #132 — the dashboard list and the per-section enrolled probe that drive the home page and the Join/Leave button.

Closes #121
Closes #114

## Summary
- \`GET /api/me/courses\` (\`ListMyEnrollments\`) — returns every section the viewer is enrolled in with compact section + course + school summaries. Optional \`term\` and \`role\` filters. No pagination.
- \`GET /api/courses/{course_id}/sections/{section_id}/members/me\` (\`CheckMembership\`) — per-section enrolled probe; always 200 with \`{enrolled, role, joined_at}\` (nulls when not enrolled).

## Design notes
- **Both endpoints live on \`CoursesHandler\`** — same package owns \`course_members\`, no new handler struct, composite untouched.
- **\`CheckMembership\` reuses \`assertCourseAndSection\`** from #132 so 'Course not found' / 'Section not found' messaging stays identical to join/leave. Critical contract: non-membership is \`200 {enrolled:false}\` — never 404 — so the frontend can distinguish 'not enrolled' from 'section deleted'.
- **\`ListMyEnrollments\` uses single fixed sort** \`(term DESC, dept ASC, number ASC)\`. Optional filters via \`sqlc.narg\`. Defensive role/term re-validation in the service since oapi-codegen does not validate query enums at the wrapper layer (only path UUIDs).
- **Compact embedded payloads**: \`EnrollmentSchoolSummary\` is just \`{id, acronym}\` — full school info lives on the course detail endpoint and would bloat the dashboard.
- **Explicit JSON nulls** on \`MembershipCheckResponse.role\`/\`joined_at\` (pointer types in generated struct + \`nullable: true\` schema) so the frontend can destructure safely.

## Commits
1. \`chore(openapi)\` — spec + 501 stubs
2. \`feat(db)\` — sqlc \`ListMyEnrollments\` + \`GetMembership\`
3. \`feat(courses)\` — domain types, params, mapper, service methods, repo wiring, mocks regen
4. \`feat(handlers)\` — replace 501 stubs with real implementations + response mappers
5. \`test(courses)\` — service + handler ACs
6. \`docs\` — regenerate openapi sidebar

## Test plan
- [x] \`go test -race ./...\` green locally
- [x] \`make lint\` clean
- [ ] Dev + stage GitHub Actions deploys green
- [ ] Staging matrix:
  - \`GET /me/courses\` with no enrollments → \`{enrollments:[]}\`
  - join → \`GET /me/courses\` returns single enrollment with hydrated section/course/school
  - \`?term=Spring%202026\` returns matching, \`?term=Fall%202099\` returns empty
  - \`?role=admin\` → 400 with role-detail message
  - \`?term=\` (31 chars) → 400 with term-detail message
  - \`GET .../members/me\` not joined → \`200 {enrolled:false, role:null, joined_at:null}\`
  - join → \`GET .../members/me\` → \`200 {enrolled:true, role:"student", joined_at:...}\`
  - 404 unknown course / unknown section / cross-course
  - 401 without JWT, 400 for malformed UUIDs

## Summary

Three UX bugs from the 102/147 run:

1. **3-min clock started at exam creation, not bot pickup** — copy-paste + bot pickup latency could eat 30-60s before the bot saw question 1. Now `expires_at` is bumped to `NOW() + 3min` on the bot's first `GET /arena/test/:examId`; atomic via `first_fetched_at` so duplicate/retry fetches don't reset the clock twice. author: garyocean428
body:
## Summary

After PR #491 fixed the historical-data fetcher, production logs (Railway deploy `38ef87db`, commit `8473e94`) show the pipeline is now running on real data — strategies are generating real trades and the gate is evaluating real metrics:

```
[SLE] Backtest FAIL: sle_1776501686134_158ttaa2r — backtest_gate_failed:
  totalTrades 2 < 30; sharpe -0.18 < 0.8; sortino -0.14 < 1.2; calmar -0.24 < 1.5; oos.profitFactor 0.00 < 1.1
```

But the generated signal genomes only fire 1-2 entries per backtest window (≈6,048 candles on 5m × 21 days). The 30-trade minimum is unreachable until the genome layer evolves to produce more sensitive signals.

## Fix

- `BACKTEST_MIN_TRADES: 30 → 10`
- `OOS_MIN_PROFIT_FACTOR: 1.1 → 1.0` (OOS must break even; edge-proof carried by in-sample Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar/PF)

## Why this is still safe

The multi-metric gate (Sharpe ≥ 0.8, Sortino ≥ 1.2, Calmar ≥ 1.5, PF ≥ 1.3, DD ≤ 20%) still rejects noise. A 10-trade minimum paired with those gates is comparable to the original plan's PAPER_MIN_TRADES — it's a reasonable "first-pass viability" floor.

## Test plan

- [x] 484 API tests pass
- [x] `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.build.json` clean
- [ ] Post-deploy: at least one strategy with 10+ trades passes all gates within 2-3 cycles

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Relax backtest promotion gate thresholds to allow low-frequency but statistically filtered strategies to pass an initial viability check.

Enhancements:
- Lower the minimum backtest trade count from 30 to 10 while retaining the existing multi-metric risk/quality gate.
- Reduce the required out-of-sample profit factor threshold from 1.1 to 1.0 so OOS performance only needs to be breakeven when in-sample metrics are strong.

Tests:
- Update promotion engine tests to reflect the relaxed trade-count and out-of-sample profit-factor thresholds.

2.2. Подключение JavaScript, проверка навыков работы с базовыми концепциями языка

- [x] 2.2.1. Подключить сервис показа текущего курса

В блоке где показываются курсы валют необходимо вывести значения используя сторонний сервис API.
Зарегистрироваться на любом доступном стороннем сайте для получения валют. Например: [https://app.exchangerate-api.com/dashboard.](https://app.exchangerate-api.com/dashboard) По запросу GET получаем текущий курс по отношению к RUB.
Всего необходимо вывести 6 валют, 2 основные это USD, EUR, остальные на ваш выбор. Также необходимо обновлять актуальный курс каждые 15 минут.
Подумайте над тем, как сделать универсальный запрос на получение разных валют и также любого количества валют.

- [x] 2.2.2. Подключить сервис показа текущих новостей

- [x] 2.2.3.1. Подключить сторонний API

Необходимо зарегистрироваться на https://newsapi.org/, после чего сконфигурировать свой уникальный ключ, после выбрать запрос "Top business headlines in the US right now".
В запросе приходит список последних новостей.
Важно! Количество запросов в день ограничено, всего 100 штук, необходимо это учитывать при разработке. 
В карточке новости выводятся поля:

urlToImage
title
url (для перехода на страницу с новостью)
description
Если у изображения отображается битая ссылка и если в поле description вместо текста приходит разметка, то это необходимо отфильтровать перед выводом.
Ссылка на новость должна открываться в новой вкладке.
Количество новостей не ограничено, но не меньше 20.

- [x] 2.2.3.2. Реализовать слайдер для пролистывания новостей

Допустимая ширина прокрутки 500px.

500px складываются из:

320px - ширина предпоследней карточки на макете
80px - отступ до следующей карточки
100px - обрезанная 4 карточка на макете
Обрезанная карточка уведомляет пользователя о том, что новости еще дальше можно листать.
Последняя карточка из списка должна быть показана полностью.
Сделать блокировку кнопок на первой и последнем элементе.

Критерии принятия Pull Request:

Корректно отображён вывод курса валют.
Корректно отображён вывод списка новостей
При переключении слайдера (назад, вперёд) ничего не ломается

body:
Several mostly unrelated improvements for #6442:

* 8080a68: moves the responsibility of allocating channel IDs to application
  * makes it possible to check if they are unused and unique across interfaces
  * helper struct for allocating sequential ids with random start
  * Mux no longer needs to hold onto CredentailVerifier/CredentialStore, simplifying type signatures a bit
* fd1d2a8: adds `host::Channel` and `device::Channel` type aliases for shorter type signatures
* 851f362: channels now keep track of how many times they retransmitted the current message
  * also ported the python function for computing ACK timeouts
  * application still needs to keep track of when to request retransmission, mainly because there is no universal `time::Instant` and it's probably not worth it to introduce another type parameter
* 1c2679b: channels remember the handshake pairing state and peer's static pubkey
* 71fc240: adds support for sending `transport_error` messages
  * device sends `DECRYPTION_FAILED` when AEAD tag verification fails
* 876ee8e: log channel numbers in hexadecimal

## Summary

Architecture audit запущенный через wave-pipeline (9 параллельных спеков, 5 волн). Результат: 954 тестов зелёных, lint чистый, build успешный.

- **Layering (spec-01):** извлечён service layer — `lib/classification-service.ts`, `lib/matching/pair-analyzer.ts`, `lib/pipeline.ts`; god-роуты `classify` (107→42 LOC) и `match` (427→80 LOC) стали тонкими адаптерами
- **Security (spec-02):** CSRF-защита добавлена на 4 незащищённых AI-роута (`recap`, `counterparty`, `draft-quote`, `draft-reply`) + тесты на `validateCsrf`
- **Performance (spec-03):** p-limit на Gmail (10 concurrent) и OpenAI (3 concurrent); O(1) Map-lookup вместо O(n²) в match; `updateSessionField` для частичной записи сессии
- **API contract (spec-04):** zod-валидация на `draft-quote`/`draft-reply`; `/api/v1/:path*` rewrites для версионирования
- **State mgmt (spec-05):** eager `expireOldSessions()` sweep в `createSession`; JSDoc на `SESSION_TTL_MS`
- **Extensibility (spec-06):** `lib/prompts.ts` 712 строк → barrel + 7 domain-файлов; `lib/freshness.ts` hardcoded switch → data-driven `FRESHNESS_CONFIG`
- **Testing (spec-07):** SQLite-backed session CRUD тесты (5 новых)
- **Team & DX (spec-08):** убран `ignoreBuildErrors`/`ignoreDuringBuilds`; `lib/ui-render.tsx` — shared detail-page helpers; `extractStr` в `lib/parsing-utils.ts`; `commission.ts` без `: any`
- **Deployment (spec-09):** CI `continue-on-error` убран; Node.js 20→22 в CI; `ecosystem.config.js` динамический cwd

The CEO plan includes a line-level supersedes list (Adhan reframe, engine-vs-reference clarification, v1 phasing sync, etc.) to apply to the approved design doc on merge. See `~/.gstack/projects/aitasadduq-aynama-prayer-times/ceo-plans/2026-04-17-muslim-prayer-app.md`.

## Summary

- Ship PDF-to-MasterProfile ingest end-to-end: `unpdf` text extraction, OpenRouter structured-output parsing, Zod-validated save scoped to the session user.
- Add `/api/profile/ingest`, `/api/profile` (GET/PUT), `src/ingestion/pdf.ts`, `src/ai/{client,prompts,ingestProfile}.ts`, and an Import-from-PDF control on the profile page.
- Wire `profile.service.ts` to the real API; `ProfileStatusCard` and `/dashboard` now handle the "no profile yet" case.

## TDD evidence

Visible in `git log` on this branch:
1. `test(phase-1.a): RED — extractText reads text from a PDF buffer` → failing test, committed alone.
2. `feat(phase-1.a): GREEN — extractText wraps unpdf with typed error contract` → minimal impl, test passes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 32 files / 408 tests green, including 10 new API-route tests, 4 new ingestion tests, 8 new fetch-mocked service tests, and 3 new profile-page tests.
- [x] `npm run build` — Next.js build passes; new routes listed as dynamic.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean (pre-existing `no-console` warnings only).
- [x] `npm run format:check` — all files formatted.
- [ ] Smoke: sign in locally, upload a real resume PDF on `/profile`, verify parsed JSON + save. *(Deferred — done tomorrow with Dako.)*
- [ ] `npm run test:integration` — deferred; requires a dedicated Neon test branch. Unit + route handler coverage exercises the FK path today.

## Security

- A01: `auth()` runs before every DB write; `userId` is session-only, never from body.
- A02: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` read from env; never echoed in logs.

author: mryel00
body:
Programs like Crowsnest set some default values. Using `store_true` does not allow to negate this flag. This made problems with e.g. `disable_webrtc` for Pi5.
I refactored the WebRTC logic to disable it, if `_hw_encoder_available` is `False`.

Renamed `use-sw-jpg-encoder` to `use-sw-encoder` which also disables WebRTC. This option is still needed, if you want to increase the image size beyond the capabilities of the HW encoder of a Pi.
This also disables WebRTC that it can actually start up with a higher resolution.

I also added the new option `force-webrtc` to force the start of a WebRTC stream, no matter the circumstances. This will still use the HW encoder and therefore fail the startup, if the resolution exceeds the HW capabilities.
But this option will enable support for WebRTC on the Pi5, even if it isn't recommended.

This PR should not break existing setups, but we might remove deprecated options in the future.

Swaps the bare `\!=` in the state CSRF check inside `_run_authorization_flow` for `secrets.compare_digest`. author: veronikya
body:
# PR: feat(base-ui): add drag-to-resize column widths persisted in localStorage

## Summary

Adds **drag-to-resize column widths** to the base-ui Table component. User-adjusted widths are persisted in browser `localStorage` and automatically restored on page reload.

- Users can resize columns by dragging the vertical handle on the right edge of any column header
- Width data is stored in `localStorage`, keyed by `tableId + viewId` — each view maintains its own independent column widths
- No backend calls — purely local persistence
- Live preview during drag; only written to localStorage on mouse-up (avoids excessive writes)
- Column width priority: live drag preview > localStorage > backend view meta > API column.width > default 235px
- Minimum column width enforced at 80px

## Changes

### `base-ui/src/plugins/GridViewPlugin/utils/columnWidthStorage.ts` _(new)_

localStorage wrapper module with three exported functions:

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `getColumnWidths(tableId, viewId)` | Read column widths for a given table + view |
| `saveColumnWidths(tableId, viewId, widths)` | Persist column widths to localStorage |
| `clearColumnWidths(tableId, viewId)` | Clear column widths for a given table + view |

Storage key format: `serenibase_col_widths_<tableId>_<viewId>`

### `base-ui/src/plugins/GridViewPlugin/hooks/useTableViewConfig.ts`

- New `tableId` parameter (used to build the localStorage key)
- New `localColumnWidths` state (loaded from localStorage on mount)
- New `handleColumnWidthChange(columnId, width)` — updates local state and writes to localStorage; does **not** call the backend
- Automatically loads saved widths from localStorage when switching views

### `base-ui/src/plugins/GridViewPlugin/components/Table/Table.tsx`

- New resize state: `resizingColumnIndex`, `liveColumnWidths` (for live preview during drag)
- New `handleResizeMouseDown` — on mousedown, registers global `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners; mousemove updates `liveColumnWidths` for real-time preview; mouseup calls `handleColumnWidthChange` to persist
- Refactored `columnWidths` useMemo with 5-level priority (see Summary)
- Added resize handle inside each column header (1px vertical line on the right edge; hover highlight; `cursor: col-resize`)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Open any table, drag the vertical handle on a column header edge — column width updates in real time
- [ ] Stop dragging and refresh the page — column width is preserved (localStorage working)
- [ ] Switch views — each view has its own independent column widths
- [ ] Clear localStorage and refresh — column widths fall back to backend defaults
- [ ] Minimum width constraint: dragging below 80px clamps to 80px
- [ ] All 5774 tests pass (`pnpm test -- --run`)

## Verification

```bash
cd base-ui
pnpm lint          # 0 errors
pnpm type-check    # no new type errors
pnpm test -- --run # 5774 passed
```

body: ## 背景 按要求对 P12（运输需求）进行功能、逻辑、安全审计，并修复发现的问题。 ## 审计发现与修复 ### 1) 安全漏洞：中台接口未鉴权 - 问题：`/api/admin/transport-demand/**` 可匿名访问。 - 修复：新增并启用统一中台鉴权： - `AdminAuthProperties` - `AdminAuthInterceptor` - `WebMvcConfig` - `application.yml` 增加： - `huodaizi.admin.auth.enabled: true` - `huodaizi.admin.auth.token: change-this-admin-token` ### 2) 安全漏洞：异常处理 HTTP 语义与信息泄露 - 问题：异常处理直接返回 `ApiResponse`，HTTP 语义不完整，500 可能泄露内部信息。 - 修复： - `GlobalExceptionHandler` 改为 `ResponseEntity>` - 错误码映射：401/400/404/500 - 500 不回传内部异常细节 - `ErrorCode` 增加 `UNAUTHORIZED`、`AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR` ### 3) 逻辑缺陷：服务需求筛选归一化不一致 - 问题：`matchServiceNeed` 中候选值做了 normalize，但筛选值未统一归一化，筛选稳定性不足。 - 修复：对 `serviceNeedFilter` 同步 normalize 后比较，避免大小写/空白差异导致匹配失败。 ### 4) 输入校验一致性 - 问题：`TransportDemandAdminController.pin` 使用 `IllegalArgumentException`，与模块内业务异常体系不一致。 - 修复：统一改为 `BaseException(BAD_REQUEST, "pinned 不能为空")`。 ### 5) 工程补充 - 新增 `backend/.gitignore`（`/target/`, `*.log`）。 - README 增补中台 token 鉴权说明。 ## 新增测试 新增 `TransportDemandAuditIntegrationTest`，覆盖： - 公共详情返回联系人与手机号脱敏 - 公共列表按 origin/destination/goodsCategory/vehicleType/timeliness/invoiceNeed 筛选 - 中台无 token 返回 401 - 中台有 token 返回 200 - 非法 status 返回 400 - pin 缺少 `pinned` 返回 400 ## 验证结果 - `mvn -q clean test` ✅ - `mvn -q -DskipTests package` ✅ - 运行态 smoke ✅ - `/api/v1/transport-demand/filters` 200 - `/api/v1/transport-demand` 200（筛选正确） - `/api/v1/transport-demand/{id}` 200（脱敏正确） - `/api/admin/transport-demand` 无 token -> 401 - `/api/admin/transport-demand` 有 token -> 200 - 非法 status -> 400 - pin 缺失 pinned -> 400 ## 风险说明 - 当前仍为内存仓储 MVP，重启后数据重置（本次不改变该约束）。

Buatlah sebuah file **`Buku-Ajar-Multimedia-Digital-Interaktif.md`** yang merupakan Buku Ajar lengkap dengan struktur sebagai berikut:

### STRUKTUR BUKU AJAR

- Program Studi: D4 Teknologi Rekayasa Multimedia
- Institusi: Politeknik Negeri Lhokseumawe

#### PRAKATA
Prakata harus berisi bagian-bagian berikut:

Uraikan gambaran garis besar mata kuliah Multimedia Digital dan Interaktif, mencakup topik-topik: Desain Interaksi (IxD), User Experience (UX), User-Centered Design (UCD), Prototyping & Usability Testing, Arsitektur Informasi & Wireframe, serta Produksi Aset Grafis. **B. Prasyarat Mata Kuliah**
Mata kuliah prasyarat yang relevan (misalnya: Desain Grafis, Dasar Multimedia, Pemrograman Web Dasar, atau sejenisnya — sesuaikan dengan konteks prodi D4 Teknologi Rekayasa Multimedia).

**C. Rencana Pembelajaran**
Uraikan rencana pembelajaran per pertemuan berdasarkan 5 modul di atas (masing-masing 3 jam praktikum / 150 menit). Buat tabel sederhana pertemuan dan topik.

**D. Petunjuk Penggunaan Buku Ajar**
1. Penjelasan bagi mahasiswa — cara menggunakan buku ajar ini untuk belajar mandiri dan praktikum.
2. Peran Dosen — bagaimana dosen mengelola perkuliahan dari awal hingga akhir.

**E. Capaian Pembelajaran/Kompetensi**
Berdasarkan modul-modul yang ada, capaian pembelajaran utama adalah:
- CPMK 1: Mahasiswa mampu menganalisis prinsip-prinsip Desain Interaksi dan User Experience pada produk digital.
- CPMK 2: Mahasiswa mampu merancang user interface (UI) dan user experience (UX) untuk aplikasi multimedia interaktif menggunakan proses desain yang berpusat pada pengguna.
- CPMK 3: Mahasiswa mampu membuat prototipe dan melakukan evaluasi desain (usability testing).
- CPMK 4: Mahasiswa mampu merancang arsitektur informasi dan wireframe menggunakan perangkat lunak.
- CPMK 5: Mahasiswa mampu memproduksi aset grafis (ikon, tombol, gambar) yang dioptimalkan untuk web/mobile.

**F. Bentuk Evaluasi/Umpan Balik Aktivitas Belajar**
Uraikan bentuk evaluasi: laporan praktikum, tes formatif, tugas proyek, presentasi, dan portofolio digital.

#### BAB-BAB (5 BAB)

**a. Deskripsi Singkat** — Gambaran garis besar isi bab.

**b. Relevansi** — Mengapa materi ini relevan untuk mahasiswa Teknologi Rekayasa Multimedia.

**c. Capaian Pembelajaran** — Kemampuan yang diperoleh setelah mempelajari bab ini (ambil dari tujuan praktikum di masing-masing modul).

**d. Isi BAB / Teori** — Isi materi lengkap. Ambil dan kembangkan dari bagian "Dasar Teori Singkat" dan "Langkah-langkah Praktikum" di masing-masing modul. Perluas penjelasan teorinya agar layak sebagai buku ajar (bukan hanya modul praktikum). Tambahkan penjelasan konsep, contoh, dan ilustrasi tekstual.

**e. Rangkuman** — Rangkuman materi bab.

**f. Tes Formatif** — Minimal 2 soal per bab (bisa pilihan ganda atau esai). Buat soal yang menguji pemahaman konsep.

#### BAB 1: Analisis Prinsip Desain Interaksi (IxD) dan User Experience (UX)

body:
## Summary

Three commits landing on top of the Phase 1+2 release engineering work already on `master`:

- **`build(release): auto-release on VERSION bump, tag created by CI`** — the release signal is now a commit that changes `VERSION` on `master`. CI builds, publishes to PyPI + npm, then creates `v<VERSION>` and drafts the GitHub Release. No manual `git tag`, no `gh` dispatch. `release.yml` triggers on path filter (`VERSION`, `_version.py`, `ts/package.json`), the `plan` job diffs against `HEAD~1` and short-circuits if the tag already exists on origin (idempotent), and a new `tag-release` job runs after both prod publishes succeed. `just rel-tag` stays as an emergency escape hatch; canonical flow is `just rel-prepare minor && git push`.
- **`docs(overhaul): visual + writing + diagram revamp + validator zeroed`** — Phase 5 rewrite: Mermaid diagrams + "read it when" tables on tier landing pages, decision matrices for transfer-control/structured-data/context-engineering, validator fixes (code-fence-aware heading collection, plan-tree skip), and stale-reference cleanup. Validator now reports 0 findings across `docs/` (was 70).
- **`docs(pipeline): Phase 4 — scoped method anchors, tier landing pages, code-fence validator`** — doc generator emits scoped MyST anchors (`method-<Builder>-<method>`) so Loop/FanOut/Pipeline can share `.ask`/`.build` without slug collisions; dedupes `(category, name)` pairs preferring the richer docstring; adds `--check-code-fences` validator mode. ## Summary

用户截图显示 mobile preview 视觉灾难：frame 超大、内容溢出、iframe 露在 frame 外。本 PR 修复 PhoneFrame fixed pixel sizing + iframe containment + canvas centering。

author: sebr
body:
## Summary

Fixes #393. On accounts with more than one `sprinkler_timer`, zone history for every device after the first showed `unknown` starting in 4.0.0.

**Root cause:** `_last_poll_device_histories` and `_last_poll_landscapes` in `pybhyve/client.py` were single scalar timestamps shared across all devices. The 4.0.0 coordinator fetches history/landscapes for each sprinkler sequentially on every tick — the first device updates the stamp, subsequent devices bail out at the rate-limit check milliseconds later, and their entries are never populated in `_device_histories`. `get_device_history()` then returns `None` → coordinator converts to `[]` → zone history sensor renders `unknown`.

Landscapes had the same shared-timestamp bug **plus** `self._landscapes` was a single list overwritten on each per-device fetch, so only the last device's landscape data survived regardless.

**Fix:** key both the state and the timestamps by `device_id`.

## Test plan

- [x] New `tests/test_client.py` covers:
  - Back-to-back history fetches for different devices each hit the API (regression for #393)
  - Same-device history fetch is rate-limited within the poll period
  - `force_update=True` bypasses the rate limit
  - Landscape fetches for different devices are both served
  - A zone lookup for one device does not fall through to another device's landscape list
  - Same-device landscape fetch is rate-limited
- [x] Full suite: 148 passed, 5 skipped
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean

author: copilot
body:
This PR completes the logout path for stateless JWT auth: users can explicitly log out from the UI, client auth state is cleared immediately, and protected routes are no longer reachable afterward. It also adds a secured backend logout endpoint to support current behavior and future token invalidation/audit extensions.

- **Backend: secured logout endpoint**
  - Added `POST /api/auth/logout` in `AuthController`.
  - Returns a consistent success payload:
    ```json
    { "message": "Logged out successfully" }
    ```
  - Extracts authenticated principal via `Authentication` and logs logout identity (or warns when missing), keeping the path extensible for future blacklist/revocation hooks.

- **Backend: security policy update**
  - Tightened auth allowlist in `SecurityConfig` from broad `/api/auth/**` to explicit public endpoints (`/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/register`).
  - `POST /api/auth/logout` is now protected by default under `/api/**` authentication rules.

- **UI: logout action + auth teardown**
  - Added `logoutUser(token)` API call in `authService`.
  - `AuthContext.logout` now:
    1. calls `/api/auth/logout` (best-effort),
    2. clears stored auth,
    3. clears in-memory auth state.
  - Token cleanup now removes both `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` entries for `choretrack.token`.

- **UI: logout entry point + redirect**
  - Added a `Logout` action on `DashboardPage`.
  - On click, user is redirected to `/login` after auth teardown; existing `ProtectedRoute` then blocks `/dashboard` access when unauthenticated.

- **Targeted auth coverage updates**
  - Added logout response assertions in auth controller unit tests to cover success-path contract.

Example (UI service + context flow):
```ts
// authService.ts
export const logoutUser = async (token: string): Promise<void> => {
  if (!token.trim()) return
  await fetch('/api/auth/logout', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `****** },
  })
}

// AuthContext.tsx
const logout = async () => {
  await logoutUser(token)
  clearStoredAuthToken()
  setToken('')
}
```

body:
### Motivation

- Allow users to “second” an existing timeline suggestion so they can indicate agreement without re-submitting the exact same slot.
- Ensure the aggregated master timeline reflects both original submissions and seconding support so popularity is represented accurately.
- Safely add support to existing deployments by applying a lightweight runtime migration for older databases.

### Description

- Add a `seconds` integer column to the `timeline_entries` schema and update `worker/schema.sql` to include `seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`.
- Implement a runtime migration helper `ensureTimelineSecondsColumn(env)` that checks `PRAGMA table_info(timeline_entries)` and runs `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` when needed.
- Add a new API endpoint `POST /api/timeline-entries/:id/second` that accepts a JSON `delta` (`1` or `-1`) and updates `seconds` with `UPDATE timeline_entries SET seconds = MAX(0, COALESCE(seconds,0) + ?)`.
- Include `seconds` in `GET /api/timeline-entries` responses and change master aggregation to `SUM(1 + COALESCE(t.seconds, 0)) AS totalVotes` so seconding impacts the master timeline.

body:
## Overview
This PR completes the frontend React application for the AWS Architect tool. It finalizes the user flow from initial prompt submission through dynamic diagram rendering and secure AWS credential collection.

## Key Features
- 💬 **Live Chat Interface:** Fully styled dark-mode chat with typing indicators, timestamps, and auto-scrolling functionality.
- 🔌 **WebSocket Integration:** Connects to the live API Gateway with robust error handling (shows UI alerts if the backend handshake fails or disconnects).
- 📊 **Dynamic Diagram Rendering:** Uses `react-markdown` and `mermaid.js` to automatically parse and render architecture graphs sent by Bedrock.
- 🔒 **AWS Auth Modal (Steps 6 & 9):** A popup that triggers when the user clicks "Confirm & Deploy Architecture" to collect their deployment credentials.
- ✅ **Input Validation & Error UI:** Client-side Regex validation for AWS Access Key IDs (20 chars, `AKIA`/`ASIA` prefix) and Secret Access Keys (40 chars). Includes custom red warning boxes for invalid inputs.
- 🧪 **Built-in UI Simulator:** Added an `IS_TEST_MODE` toggle at the top of `App.jsx`. When `true`, it bypasses the WebSocket and simulates backend delays/diagram generation for easy UI testing.

## How to Test
1. Pull down this branch and run `npm run dev`.
2. Open `src/App.jsx` and verify `const IS_TEST_MODE = true;` is set at the top.
3. Submit a prompt to see the simulated Mermaid diagram generation.
4. Click "Confirm & Deploy" to test the modal. Try entering fake credentials to see the Regex error validation. 
5. Enter validly formatted credentials to see the simulated deployment success message.
6. Once the backend API Gateway is live, switch `IS_TEST_MODE = false;` to connect to the real server!

author: edbertchan
body:
## Summary
Fix the Docker comprehensive fixture image setup so it works when CI is running on `master` after merge.

## Root Cause
The fixture builder always did `git branch "${CURRENT_BRANCH}"` followed by `git checkout "${CURRENT_BRANCH}"` inside `/app`. The base image already seeds a git repo on `master`, so post-merge push runs failed when `CURRENT_BRANCH=master` with:

`fatal: a branch named 'master' already exists`

PR runs passed because they used a non-`master` branch name.

## Change
Replace branch creation plus checkout with:

`git checkout -B "${CURRENT_BRANCH}"`

That keeps the fixture setup idempotent for both PR and post-merge push runs.

## Verification
- Reproduced the failing git sequence for an existing `master` branch.
- Verified that `git checkout -B master` succeeds in the same state.
- Docker daemon was not available locally in this environment, so I could not rerun the full Docker CI job here.

body: ## Summary Devin Review caught that the "no-limit" queries in PR #80 weren't actually no-limit. Supabase's PostgREST config sets `max_rows = 1000` globally (), so any query without an explicit `.limit()` silently caps at 1000 rows. Same class of silent-undercount bug PR #79 produced at 500 — just pushed to 1000 instead of fixed. ## Fix Push the house filter into the PostgREST query via the inner-join dot path (works because both relations already use `!inner`), then re-add the explicit `.limit(CAP + 1)` cap. With the filter applied at the DB layer the cap is now correct ("manager's houses, up to 501 rows") and matches the admin-path semantics. Client-side post-filter is removed since the DB does it. - `ChoreReviewsStatTile`: `.in("rotation_assignment.rotation.house_id", houseFilter)` - `LeaveRequestsStatTile`: `.in("resident.house_id", houseFilter)` ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] As a manager with 1–2 assigned houses, verify the Chore Reviews + Leave Requests dashboard tiles match the actual count on `/chores?tab=to-review` and `/leave-requests?status=pending` filtered to those houses. - [ ] PostgREST nested-dot filter (`rotation_assignment.rotation.house_id`) actually filters — if it doesn't (some supabase-js versions/configs have quirks with deep paths), the filtered count will come back empty. Sanity-check by comparing against a known non-empty manager state. - [ ] Admin (unfiltered) path still caps at `500+` when global queue exceeds 500. ### Notes - Pure correctness fix. No schema. No UI copy change. - Addresses Devin Review comment id 3106269216 on merged PR #80. - If PostgREST's two-level dot filter on `rotation_assignment.rotation.house_id` turns out not to apply (haven't been able to smoke-test against prod data from here), the fallback is to raise `max_rows` server-side or use an explicit `.limit(10000)` with a longer cap — happy to follow up if so. - No CI run per your preference. author: alicelr
body:
Adds full support for Amiga paths to path.c functions, particularly:

- Amiga-style roots: these are much more permissive than DOS/Windows roots and even the modified DOS-like roots used in some console SDKs and in certain places in Linux et al. (everything prior to the first : is included in the root). Additionally, there should be no slashes following the :, unlike with DOS-like roots.

- Amiga parent directory: zero-length directory tokens navigate to the parent directory, instead of ".." like most other places. This includes "/" and "somedir//", but not "somedir/". This effectively means that Amiga paths can't be slash-cleaned until path_navigate is performed. "/" is now presented in the file manager instead of "..".

- Amiga "." and ".." are completely normal files, so let the file manager rename/delete these.

author: dratner
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two root-cause triggers identified in the stalling analysis (maestro-issues `stalling-triggers-analysis.md`):

- **Trigger 1 — Bootstrap race / missing make targets**: When a project's Makefile lacks a `test` target (common during bootstrap), `make test` returned exit code 2 which was treated as a test failure, blocking the coder in a retry loop. Now detects missing targets via stderr pattern matching (`ErrTargetNotFound` sentinel) and marks tests as `skipped` instead of `failed`. The skip status flows through to code review evidence so the architect has full visibility. Verification/probing still runs after a skip.

- **Trigger 2 — Git object corruption cascade**: Mirror corruption (from interrupted fetches, macOS filesystem artifacts, or Docker bind mount issues) propagated silently into workspace clones, causing stale-object errors during commit/push. Now runs `git fsck` after mirror updates and workspace clones to catch corruption early. Consolidates validation through `mirror.ValidateRepo` (exported) for the mirror-manager path and `gitRunner` for mock-compatible workspace checks. Expands commit-failure classification with three new patterns from MAE-0006/0007 incidents. Adds pre-staging cleanup of macOS filesystem artifacts (`.DS_Store`, `._*`).

## Changes

### Trigger 1 (commit 1)
- `pkg/build/build_api.go` — `ErrTargetNotFound` sentinel, `Skipped`/`SkipReason` fields on `Response`, stderr tee in `runMakeTarget`, `isMakeTargetMissing` detection
- `pkg/coder/coder_fsm.go` — `KeyTestStatus`, `KeyTestSkipReason` state data keys
- `pkg/coder/testing.go` — `buildTestResult` struct replacing `(bool, string, error)` return; skip branch still runs lint/verification
- `pkg/coder/code_review.go` — Surfaces skip status in completion evidence for architect
- `pkg/coder/prepare_merge.go` — Updated caller for struct return
- `pkg/build/build_api_test.go` — `TestIsMakeTargetMissing` (6 subtests), `TestErrTargetNotFoundSkipsInResponse`
- `pkg/coder/code_review_test.go` — `TestBuildCompletionEvidence_TestsSkipped`, updated existing tests

### Trigger 2 (commit 2)
- `pkg/mirror/manager.go` — Exported `ValidateRepo` (full fsck, dropped `--connectivity-only`), post-update revalidation with recovery
- `pkg/coder/clone.go` — Post-update mirror revalidation in `ensureMirrorClone`, workspace fsck after fetch in `createFreshClone`
- `pkg/tools/build_tools.go` — 3 new error classification patterns, pre-staging `.DS_Store`/`._*` cleanup
- `pkg/build/executor.go` — `StderrOutput` field on `MockExecutor`

## Test plan

- [x] `TestCreateFreshClone_Success` / `TestCreateFreshClone_CleansExistingDirectory` — Workspace fsck via mock gitRunner

body:
💡 **What:**
Added `aria-controls` bindings to the collapsible dropdown in the `ProjectSelector` and the project groups in the `Sidebar`.

🎯 **Why:**
These elements function as disclosure widgets. While they correctly updated `aria-expanded` to communicate their state to screen readers, they lacked the `aria-controls` attribute necessary to programmatically link the trigger button to the collapsible content panel. This omission causes accessibility linters to flag the components and prevents assistive technologies from correctly guiding users to the expanded content.

📸 **Before/After:**
*   **Before:** Trigger buttons lacked `aria-controls`.
*   **After:** Trigger buttons now dynamically point to their target panel's `id`.

♿ **Accessibility:**
*   Ensured complete implementation of the W3C WAI-ARIA authoring practices for disclosure widgets.
*   Utilized React's `useId()` hook in `sidebar.tsx` to generate globally unique, deterministic IDs for dynamically rendered groups, eliminating duplicate ID warnings.
*   Employed conditional rendering for `aria-controls` (`aria-controls={isOpen ? 'id' : undefined}`) to prevent the attribute from pointing to a non-existent DOM element when the content is unmounted, addressing a common automated a11y checker failure.

author: parasol-aser
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3177.

The public Android JNI decoder wrapper (`android_jni/avifandroidjni/src/main/jni/libavif_jni.cc`) accepts a caller-supplied signed `int length` at every direct-`ByteBuffer` entry point and forwards it, unchecked, into the native `size_t size` boundary of `avifDecoderSetIOMemory()`. A negative length (e.g. `-1`) or a negative-as-int oversize (e.g. `0x80000000`) sign-extends to a near-`SIZE_MAX` value; the parser then trusts the inflated advertised size and reads past the real direct-buffer allocation. ASan reports a `heap-buffer-overflow` in `avifROStreamRead` (see the stack in the issue).

This PR enforces the contract at the JNI boundary — where the signed `int` enters — so that every downstream caller of `avifDecoderSetIOMemory()` stays free to pass any `size_t` it likes.

### Changes

- **New `ValidateDirectBuffer()` helper** in the `libavif_jni.cc` anonymous namespace that:
  - Rejects `length < 0` before any cast.
  - Reads `GetDirectBufferCapacity(encoded)` once and rejects non-direct buffers (`capacity < 0`) and `length > capacity` (strict `>`).
  - Rejects a `nullptr` address from `GetDirectBufferAddress()`.
  - Casts to `size_t` only after the checks pass; returns the validated `(buffer, size_t size)` pair.
- **Hardened all four public JNI entry points** that consume a direct `ByteBuffer` and an explicit length: `isAvifImage`, `getInfo`, `decode`, and `createDecoder`. Each now early-exits with its clean-failure value (`false` / `0`) when validation fails.
- **`CreateDecoderAndParse()` signature** changed from `int length` to `size_t length` so the signed-to-unsigned sign-extension is gone from the internal helper too. All four call sites updated.
- **New Android instrumentation regression test** `AvifDecoderLengthValidationTest` covering:
  - The two issue-named boundary values (`length = -1`, `length = Integer.MIN_VALUE`).
  - `length = capacity + 1` and `length = Integer.MAX_VALUE` (positive-but-oversized).
  - Non-direct (heap-backed) buffers.
  - Boundary cases that must still succeed: `length == capacity`, `length == 0`, and a valid image through `AvifDecoder.create()` / `AvifDecoder.getInfo()`.
  - Every case verifies the clean-failure contract (`false` / `null`) instead of a crash.

### Scope and non-goals

- `src/read.c`, `src/stream.c` — **unchanged**. The crash manifests there, but the parser is trusting an already-bad size handed to it. Fixing it lower down would silently paper over other callers of `avifDecoderSetIOMemory()` that are free to pass a large `size_t` deliberately.
- `AvifDecoder.java` public API surface — **unchanged**. The issue's secondary suggestion of deprecating the `int length` overloads in favor of `encoded.remaining()`-driven variants is deliberately not taken here; it would be a source-incompatible change, and the issue frames it as secondary hardening. Happy to do that as a follow-up if maintainers want it.
- No new linker deps, no new JNI reflection lookups, no C++ standard bump.

## Test plan

- [x] **Repro confirmed pre-fix.** Against `b357f08` (current `main`), the 8-byte truncated-`ftyp` payload with `length = -1` or `length = 0x80000000` produces the ASan `heap-buffer-overflow` at `avifROStreamRead` → `avifParseFileTypeBox` → `avifParse` → `avifDecoderParse` (matches the issue).
- [x] **Repro cleared post-fix at the JNI boundary.** With `ValidateDirectBuffer()` in place, the same inputs through `AvifDecoder.getInfo` / `decode` / `isAvifImage` / `create` return the clean-failure value (`false` / `null`) without entering the parser. Verified with a simulated-JNI-validation harness that mirrors the new helper before calling `avifDecoderSetIOMemory()`.
- [x] **Parser contract unchanged.** Calling `avifDecoderSetIOMemory()` directly with `(size_t)-1` still crashes as before — expected; the fix is at the JNI boundary, not in the parser. This is intentionally not a behavior change for non-JNI callers.
- [ ] **Android instrumentation suite.** Run `AvifDecoderLengthValidationTest` on an Android emulator/device, e.g.:
    ```sh
    cd android_jni && ./gradlew :avifandroidjni:connectedDebugAndroidTest \
      --tests org.aomedia.avif.android.AvifDecoderLengthValidationTest
    ```
    Every test case must pass. I don't have an Android device/emulator in this environment to run the instrumentation suite myself; maintainers with CI access should confirm. The tests reuse the existing `avif/fox.profile0.8bpc.yuv420.avif` asset already shipped under `androidTest/assets` for the happy-path cases.
- [ ] **Build hygiene.** `./android_jni/gradlew :avifandroidjni:assembleDebug` must continue to link cleanly after the `CreateDecoderAndParse` signature change. `-Wsign-compare` / `-Wconversion` remain clean across the edited block (the helper uses an explicit `static_cast<jlong>(length)` for the capacity comparison).

### Boundary behavior verified by the test matrix

| Entry point | `length` | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `getInfo` | `-1` | `false`, no crash |
| `getInfo` | `Integer.MIN_VALUE` | `false`, no crash |
| `getInfo` | `capacity + 1` (9) | `false`, no crash |
| `getInfo` | `Integer.MAX_VALUE` | `false`, no crash |
| `getInfo` | `capacity` (8, truncated ftyp) | `false` (parser — truncated data control) |
| `getInfo` | `0` (empty direct buffer) | `false` (parser — not short-circuited at JNI) |
| `getInfo` | valid image, honest length | `true` (happy path guard) |
| `decode` | `-1` / `MIN_VALUE` / `cap+1` / `MAX_VALUE` | `false`, no crash |
| `isAvifImage` | truncated ftyp / heap-backed / empty | `false`, no crash |
| `create` | truncated / heap-backed / empty | `null` |
| `create` | valid image | non-`null` (happy path guard) |

author: ediksimonian
body:
## Request
> create a joke command that I can pass a theme to. Example /joke about someone coming late or /joke about python

## Changes
- **`bot/ta/jokes.py`** (new): `generate_joke(theme, group_key)` calls the LLM with a short system prompt ("one clean, 3-sentence joke, no preamble"). Honors the per-group active model so `/model <name>` switches apply. Truncates the theme to `MAX_THEME_LEN=300` chars so students can't smuggle a novel into the prompt. Returns `None` on LLM error or empty reply.
- **`bot/ta/admin.py`**: routes `/joke` above the admin gate (same tier as `/feedback`) so students in groups aren't silently filtered by the non-admin-command delete branch. Posts the joke back to the same chat (group or DM). Command message is intentionally NOT deleted — comedy wants the setup visible. Falls back to a friendly "couldn't think of one" message if generation fails.
- **`bot/ta/commands.py`**: adds `/joke [theme]` under a new **Fun** section in `/help`.

## Assumptions
- **Open to all users** (students + admins), not admin-only. The example `/joke about someone coming late` reads like something a student might type. If admin-only is preferred, move the dispatch into `commands.py` and register it with `@_register("joke")` instead.
- **Command message stays visible** in groups (breaks the usual "delete the command" convention). Rationale: a bare punchline with no setup is confusing; seeing `student: /joke about python` → `bot: <joke>` reads more naturally.
- **No rate limit / no history**: jokes are cheap one-shot LLM calls; not worth plumbing through `ta_rate_check_and_inc` or appending to history.

## Tests
- **`tests/test_ta_jokes.py`** (new, 7 tests):
  - theme passed verbatim into the user prompt
  - empty theme produces a generic "tell me a joke" prompt
  - over-long themes are truncated at `MAX_THEME_LEN`
  - per-group active model overrides `DEFAULT_MODEL`
  - no `group_key` → `DEFAULT_MODEL` and `get_active_model` is not called
  - LLM exception → returns `None`
  - whitespace-only LLM reply → returns `None`
- **`tests/test_ta_admin.py`** (5 new router-level tests):
  - student `/joke about python` in a group → joke posted, command NOT deleted, admin dispatch NOT called, LLM Q&A path NOT called
  - `/joke` in DM → posted to user's chat
  - `/joke` with no args → `generate_joke("")` (empty theme)
  - `generate_joke` returns `None` → apology fallback message containing "try again"
  - admin `/joke` also works (same path, no dispatch)
- `make test` result: **397 passed**

author: jayhesselberth
body:
## Summary

- **Pure-Rust reference-compressed cSRA decode** — `seq_restore_read` + `align_restore_read` reimplemented from ncbi-vdb's C source. `sracha fastq` on VDB-3418 is md5-identical to `fasterq-dump --split-files`.
- **vdbcache-aware reader** — `CsraCursor::open_any` routes AlignmentCursor / ReferenceCursor to whichever archive (main .sra or .sra.vdbcache) carries each table; `sracha fetch` now downloads the sidecar when SDL advertises one.
- **Narrowed `reject_if_csra`** — the iter-4 rule rejected aligned-schema archives with `CMP_BASE_COUNT > 0` + no `unaligned` marker. Those archives still carry a physical READ column and decode cleanly through the plain path. 9 of 10 past-rejected accessions from earlier random-corpus runs now produce FASTQ, verified against `fasterq-dump` (DRR045255 included after the race fix).
- **Incidental pipeline fix** — `spots_before` for batch N of the decode loop raced with the writer thread across the bounded channel. Archives with > 1024 blobs (e.g. DRR045255, 3.7 M spots) silently reset FASTQ defline spot numbers to 1 at spot 1,048,577. Unit-pinned + integration-pinned.
- **Actionable errors** for the two known-unsupported cSRA shapes: external refseq fetch (SRR341578-class) and fixed-length SEQUENCE without physical READ_LEN. Both point users at `fasterq-dump` for the specific archive until follow-ups land.

Scope notes:
- Existing 15 integration byte-identity tests (Illumina, aligned-schema plain, split modes, gzip, zstd, corruption) all still pass.
- 7 new cSRA integration tests + 7 new unit tests. 410 unit tests / 22 integration tests green, clippy + fmt clean.
- `sracha fastq <cSRA>.sra` honours `--split`, `--compress gzip|zstd`, `-Z/--stdout`, `-t N` via the same writer infrastructure as plain SRA.

Out of scope for this PR (tracked as follow-ups):
- External refseq fetch for SRR-prefix cSRA whose REFERENCE table has no embedded CMP_READ (SRR341578 etc.).
- Static-metadata READ_LEN synthesis for fixed-length archives that omit the physical column.
- Larger monolithic-cSRA benchmark to measure parallel speedup (VDB-3418 is too small at 12 MiB to amortize per-chunk setup).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p sracha-core --lib` — 410/410
- [x] `cargo test -p sracha-core --test pipeline -- --ignored` — 22/22 (includes `csra_full_archive_matches_fasterq_dump` and `drr045255_cross_batch_spot_numbering`)

- [x] `sracha fastq DRR045255.sra` byte-identical to `fasterq-dump --split-files` (spots 1 through 3,745,800)

author: strawgate
body:
## Summary

Merges the ingest performance experiments that achieved ~9× throughput improvement (119K → 1.12M pts/sec for 10K gauge points).

## Optimizations

### T1 — FNV-1a fingerprint hashing (4.1× baseline, 119K→494K pts/sec)
- Replaces `seriesKey()` sort+join (was 28ms per 10K pts) with FNV-1a hash fingerprint
- Incremental hashing: compute base hash per scope, extend per metric, extend per point
- Hashes 2-3 labels per point instead of all 7

### T2 — Key caching + lazy label snapshots (→ 1.12M pts/sec)  
- Per-prefix key caches (resource/scope/point) avoid string concat on every point
- `sanitizeLabelKey()` memoization (cached regex replace)
- Lazy label Map build: only construct full `Map<string,string>` on first series encounter, not per point

### T3 — Number ms timestamps (avoids per-point BigInt allocation)
- `PendingSeriesSamples.timestamps`: `bigint[]` → `number[]` (milliseconds)
- Conversion to `BigInt64Array` (nanoseconds) happens once per series at flush

## New APIs
- `ingestOtlpObject()`: fast entry point for typed OTLP object callers (avoids JSON.parse overhead)
- `ingestMetricsDocument()`: extracted helper

## Testing

164/164 tests pass. Coderabbit safety fixes from PR #97 are preserved.
